117	## §1 Decision 1 — the 93 items are LEADS, not research topics
118	
119	### §1.1 The finding
120	
121	Ruling R1 converts the 93 `items` names into research slugs by manual strip. Measured against
122	the live database:
123	
124	| | |
125	|---|---|
126	| `items` rows | 93, all `status='active'`, **all created before the 2026-08-06 reset** |
127	| names embedding a numeric determination | **28** — e.g. `A-02 Acoustic Ceiling Panels (NRC ≥0.85) in Occupied Spaces`; `E-08 Corridor Clear Width (≥1200 mm Minimum on All Primary Routes)`; `A-08 HVAC Noise Control (NC-25 Maximum in Sensitive Spaces)` |
128	| names embedding a prescriptive condition clause | **23** — e.g. `E-02 Platform Lift (Where Full Passenger Lift Not Achievable)`; `D-04 Landmarks at Every Decision Point` |
129	| overlap of those two sets | 9 |
130	| **distinct names carrying a determination** | **42 of 93** — and 42 is a floor: looser condition-words reach 49, and whole-prescription names (`A-04 Acoustic Zoning: Graduated from Arrival to Primary Occupation`) are counted by neither test |
131	| items carrying `bpc_source_slug` | 87 of 93, resolving to **27 distinct slugs, all ACTIVE** among the live 106 |
132	| pre-reset sources behind those 27 slugs | 366 distinct, of which **358 (97.8%) had no admission edge** |
133	
134	**The contamination is in the `name` column, and the name column is precisely what R1 converts
135	into a research question.** Nearly half the 93 names state an answer. Those answers rest on a
136	corpus the owner set aside on 2026-08-06 *because it could not show its work* — and the specific
137	sources behind these specific items were 97.8% unadmitted, worse than the 95% corpus-wide figure
138	that justified the reset.
139	
140	### §1.2 The second vector: the determinations are still rendered
141	
142	`DR-2026-08-06` §2 states: *"The file surfaces are untouched. `references/bpc/**`,
143	`references/bpc-reasoning/**`, `references/connections/**`, `specs/`, `site/` and `parts/`
144	remain exactly as they were, as reference."*
145	
146	That was correct and deliberate for sources. For **items** it means the determinations are live on
147	every readable surface:
148	
149	- `index.html` — 91 item-name spans on the repo's front page, values included
150	- `site/specs/` — **93 per-item HTML pages**, each `<h1>` a full determination-bearing name
151	- `parts/v10/part04.md` — the complete items table
152	- `versions/current/…_v9-0_2026-03-20.md` — prose determinations (`A-03 STC ≥35 acoustic door…`)
153	- `tools/*.html` — embedded JSON carrying item codes and full names
154	- `references/bpc-reasoning/room-acoustic-performance.md` — the sole surviving reasoning doc, and
155	  the restart plan's **first slug**: it cites item codes densely and states per-population values
156	  (`RT60 ≤ 0.3 s` for DEAF, `≤ 0.4 s` labelled *"conjecture rationally informed by literature"*)
157	  resting on REF-ids that no longer exist
158	
159	**Archiving the `items` rows quarantines none of this.** A researcher who greps the repository for
160	their slug will meet the old answer before they have logged their first search.
161	
162	### §1.3 The decision proposed
163	
164	**Apply to `items` exactly the ruling already adopted for the corpus.** `DR-2026-08-06` §4.1:
165	
166	> *"Research resuming does not restore these rows. It writes new ones under the logged-search
167	> discipline, carrying the admission edge that 95% of the frozen corpus lacked."*
168	
169	And as the restart plan puts it for the pre-reset database: *"a lead list, not a backup.
170	Consulting it to find candidate sources is legitimate; every one still has to be searched for,
171	logged, re-retrieved and admitted on its own evidence."*
172	
173	**The 93 items are a lead list of research questions. They are not research questions.** No new
174	doctrine is needed; this is the existing ruling extended to the one table that was exempted from it.
175	
176	### §1.4 The quarantine protocol — six rules
177	
178	1. **No item name becomes a slug by strip.** A slug is authored from the ICF/access-need frame
179	   first; the item list may then be consulted to check *coverage* — "did we miss a topic?" — never
180	   to supply one.
181	2. **No value crosses.** No numeric, dimension, threshold, range, or prescriptive clause from an
182	   item name, `item_axis_links.mechanism_note`, or any rendered surface may appear in a
183	   `search_executions` row, a `search_candidates` row, an admitted source's fields, or a
184	   determination. Item values live in `_archived/` and in reference surfaces only.
185	3. **Item-derived topics land as `PROVISIONAL`.** `slugs.status` already permits
186	   `'PROVISIONAL'` by CHECK constraint and **zero rows currently use it**. This needs no
187	   migration, no new column, no new table. A `PROVISIONAL` slug may be searched against; it may
188	   not carry a determination until an owner promotes it to `ACTIVE`.
189	4. **Provenance is recorded, not hidden.** `created_by_session` names the session that derived the
190	   topic; the session record names the item code it came from. The lead is auditable precisely so
191	   that a later reader can test whether it anchored the result.
192	5. **Blind-first ordering.** For any slug with a rendered predecessor — which is all 27 —
193	   the search log is written before the predecessor is read. This is not a new rule: the restart
194	   plan §5 already mandates it for `room-acoustic-performance` (*"Do not read
195	   `references/bpc-reasoning/room-acoustic-performance.md` until step 12 is complete"*). This
196	   decision generalises it from one doc to the whole reference surface.
197	6. **Dedup is real work, not hygiene.** "106 + 93 = 199 topics, no dedup" is true as a string
198	   statement and misleading as a topical one: 87 of 93 items descend from 27 existing slugs, and
199	   **13 items descend from `room-acoustic-performance` alone**. The dedup pass is a topic-modelling
200	   judgement, and it is owner-gated.
201	
202	### §1.5 A consequence R1 did not price: `jurisdictional_values`
203	
204	`DR-2026-08-06` §3 rescued `jurisdictional_values` from the reset, over an explicit correction by
205	the owner, on this reasoning:
206	
207	> *"All 109 rows carry `standard_name` **and** `source_section` — 109/109 on both… A standard cited
208	> by clause is fully located; demanding a DOI of it imports an academic model onto a class that
209	> never used one."*
210	
211	**That reasoning no longer holds, and the DR was never annotated.** Live, the table retains exactly
212	five populated columns — `jv_id`, `item_code`, `jurisdiction`, `standard_name`, `evidence_tier`.
213	**`source_section` is 0/109.** The values and locators were cleared by a later owner ruling
214	(2026-08-12), recorded only in the YAML headers: *"RETIRED TO REFERENCE-ONLY… it names which
215	document to go and get, never what it says."*
216	
217	So the table the owner personally intervened to save is now a pointer list whose **only subject
218	column is `item_code`** — and it carries a foreign key to `items`. Retiring `items` (R1, handoff
219	§6 step 8) leaves 109 rows of (jurisdiction, standard_name, tier) with nothing to be *about*, on
220	top of the FK breakage separately recorded as F1 in
221	`workplan/2026-08-19-adversarial-critique-research-restart.md`.
222	
223	**Proposed:** `DR-2026-08-06` §3 is annotated to record the 2026-08-12 clearing, and
224	`jurisdictional_values` is re-keyed to slugs — or explicitly retired — as its own decision, before
225	`items` is touched. It must not be collateral damage of a step whose stated subject is `axes`.

229	## §2 Decision 2 — the apparatus freezes until one batch lands
230	
231	### §2.1 The finding
232	
233	The repository pays for meta-work and charges for research. Measured:
234	
235	| Path | Required artifacts |
236	|---|---|
237	| Add a `workplan/*.md` | commit-message format only — **and that check is push-only, skipped on PRs** |
238	| Admit one evidence source | session id · pre-state DoD run · verbatim query log before screening · tier-ordered screening · DOI pre-check · locator re-retrieval ladder · 5 metadata fields · population-match grading · class routing · **a committed SQL migration** · DoD gate exit 0 with EXAMINED > 0 · session record · **two** pointer updates · doctrine token · attestation JSON with a written self-counterclaim |
239	
240	Meanwhile the machinery keeps a permanent "unfinished" signal alive that only apparatus work
241	appears to answer:
242	
243	- The **Stop hook** in `.claude/settings.json` runs `research_batch_dod.py --all` at *every*
244	  session close and prints *"this session closed non-compliant"*. The evidence tables are empty
245	  **by owner decision**, so this cannot be cleared by any session, research or not.
246	- **13 registered checks currently examine zero subjects**, 12 of them flagged `empty-by-decision`.
247	- The doctrine-recheck counter at `data/doctrine_recheck/working_session_counter.yaml` reads
248	  `counter: 12, last_updated: 2026-05-02` — frozen for 3.5 months, with the note *"Next periodic
249	  recheck at counter == 25."* A standing obligation with a dead odometer: it can never fire, and
250	  can always be cited as owed.
251	- The backlog grows monotonically: markers (`DEFERRED|PENDING|OPEN`) across
252	  `workplan/ governance/ decisions/` went **318 → 389 → 418** and workplan files **95 → 110 → 139**
253	  over two weeks. 23 of 163 decisions sit `review_status='PENDING'`.
254	
255	Every session-close is also contractually obliged to emit a `next_action`, and the adversarial-pass
256	convention requires each critique to run in a *fresh* session. Meta-work is self-catalysing by
257	construction.
258	
259	### §2.2 The decision proposed
260	
261	**Until `evidence_sources` holds at least one admitted source with a complete walk, the following
262	are frozen** — no new instances, corrections to existing ones excepted:
263	
264	1. No new file in `workplan/`.
265	2. No new check in `governance/check-registry.yaml`.
266	3. No new register, sweep, census, or ledger.
267	4. No adversarial pass whose subject is a plan, critique, handoff, or census. **An adversarial pass
268	   may only take as its subject a diff that wrote data or synthesis.** This single rule ends the
269	   critique→plan→critique loop; the document that precedes this one is third-order and would not
270	   have been authorised under it.
271	5. No schema migration whose purpose is frame refactoring — specifically handoff §6 steps 5 and 8,
272	   for the reasons in §1.5 and in F1/F2 of the adversarial critique.
273	
274	**Mechanically enforceable**, and cheaply: one entry in `governance/check-registry.yaml` plus one
275	script, blocking, kinds `[governance]`, failing any commit that adds a file to `workplan/` or an
276	entry to the check registry while `evidence_sources` is empty. The registry's entry schema is
277	`id / cmd / battery / kinds / level / basis / cost / min_items`, and the three attestation checks
278	are existing precedent for changeset-scoped gating. **A check that blocks new checks is the
279	smallest possible reversal of the cost gradient.**
280	
281	### §2.3 Three companion changes, each one edit
282	
283	- **`skills/session-consolidator_SKILL.md`** — make `next_action` optional, defaulting to *"none —
284	  resume the restart plan at step N"*. Delete the Step 1c heuristic that converts a plan pivot into
285	  a D-OP record. Retire the dead recheck counter.
286	- **`governance/doctrine-recheck.md` §1.3** — drop "any doctrinal-rule revision" as a recheck
287	  trigger. It makes governance edits self-breeding.
288	- **`.claude/settings.json`** — gate the Stop hook's FAIL print on `EXAMINED > 0`. *This is harness
289	  configuration and is proposed for the owner to make, not executed here.*
290	
291	### §2.4 What the freeze does not do
292	
293	It does not cull. `workplan/2026-08-18-cull-execution-plan.md` remains independent and unaffected;
294	this decision neither adopts nor rejects it. It does not retire any check — the 13 zero-subject
295	checks stay registered, and re-arm when their subjects repopulate, exactly as `DR-2026-08-06` §4.2
296	already instructs. It does not touch the R1–R15 research contract, which is the one piece of
297	apparatus that acts on research rather than on itself.
298	
299	---

304	extends that: **no schema phase is a prerequisite either.** Every input the first batch reads is

457	the gate cannot see it. Restarting research without wiring it re-mints identifiers for sources this
458	project already found and paid to verify. No live Python reads or writes `source_locators`, and no
459	registry check protects it.

461	**Doctrine.** This is not a new decision. On **2026-08-12** — six days *after* the reset — the owner
462	ruled DOIs and URLs kept, into a table whose own migration header states: *"Reference-only registry…
463	NOT an evidence table… this table only prevents duplicate lookups and names documents worth
464	sourcing,"* with the standing rule *"consumed and retired as sources are admitted."* A DOI is a
465	name, not a finding. `DR-2026-08-06` §4.1 sets the corpus aside because it *could not show its work*
466	— an argument about assertions, not identifiers. The restart plan already blesses the practice:
467	*"Consulting it to find candidate sources is legitimate; every one still has to be searched for,
468	logged, re-retrieved and admitted on its own evidence."* This section mechanises that sentence.

470	**Design.** Widen `source_locators`; do not build a new table and do not use `search_candidates`
471	(which requires `found_under_slug` and `session` NOT NULL — recovered leads have neither, and its
472	disposition vocabulary describes screening inside a logged search these rows never had).

474	```sql
475	ALTER TABLE source_locators ADD COLUMN title             TEXT;     -- re-findability, not bibliography
476	ALTER TABLE source_locators ADD COLUMN pub_year          INTEGER;
477	ALTER TABLE source_locators ADD COLUMN first_author_last TEXT;
478	ALTER TABLE source_locators ADD COLUMN lead_status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'LEAD'
479	  CHECK (lead_status IN ('LEAD','SUPERSEDED-TWIN','CONSUMED','DEAD-LOCATOR'));
480	ALTER TABLE source_locators ADD COLUMN consumed_by_ref_id TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id);
481	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_source_locators_doi_active
482	  ON source_locators (lower(doi)) WHERE doi IS NOT NULL AND lead_status='LEAD';

516	## §7 Adversarial review — preserved as a truth-instrument, abolished as a plan-instrument
517	
518	**The finding.** ≥10 adversarial passes ran in five weeks. **Not one examined research output**,
519	because there is none. The convention that each runs in a fresh session is epistemically correct and
520	is simultaneously the mechanism guaranteeing a new session per critique. Critique → plan → critique
521	is the tightest loop in this repository.
522	
523	**The precedent already exists.** `sessions/session_2026-07-26-energy-conservation-rest-points-seating-adversarial.md`
524	is the only adversarial pass ever run on research output — owner-prompted, one session, **seven
525	findings, all against the author's own admitted batch**, catching error in *both* directions (A4 a
526	T1-candidate under-tiered at T3; A5 a no-participants discussion piece over-tiered; A2 the same
527	dataset admitted twice; A3 a circular value; A6 a wrong R14 zero-yield diagnosis). Its own synthesis:
528	*"a claim pitched at a confidence the retrieval didn't earn."* **That session is the standard form.**
529	
530	**The agonist already exists and costs nothing extra.** R1–R15 already compel the authoring session
531	to file its complete affirmative case *as rows* — verbatim queries, re-retrieved locators, match
532	grades, prior expectation, named dissenter, falsification condition. There is no live debate to
533	build: the agonist's brief **is the batch's data.** The antagonist is a fresh session attacking that
534	recorded case. The cheapest agonist–antagonist mechanic is **blind-then-compare**: re-grade tier and
535	population-match independently *before* seeing the author's grades, then diff. That is precisely what
536	caught A4 and A5.
537	
538	**Eight lenses**, each naming its claim and its evidence obligation: **L1 Existence** (source
539	resolves) · **L2 Fidelity** (the source *says* what is claimed; the locator holds the value) ·
540	**L3 Independence** (same dataset twice; circular values) · **L4 Tier** (wrong in either direction,
541	incl. R5 non-English) · **L5 Population** (study vs served) · **L6 Contrary** (was "NONE FOUND" a
542	search failure) · **L7 Recognition** (Co-1 cited faithfully; would a disabled person served by this
543	recognise it) · **L8 Query-shape** (R14).
544	
545	**Adjudication without a third agent** — adding a judge adds a loop stage. Sustained and accepted →
546	row correction by migration **in the same pass**. Disputed → the cell caps at `provisional` with the
547	dispute recorded. Doctrine-level → the owner. **L5 needs no schema change**: `evidence_population_match`
548	has only `match_id` as its primary key, so a dissenting grade lands as a second row distinguished by
549	`created_by_session`, and divergent grades read as a contest.
550	
551	**Optional single migration:** an `adversarial_findings` table in which **`SURVIVED` rows are
552	mandatory** — so a zero-finding pass is auditable rather than indistinguishable from a pass that
553	never ran. That targets this repository's signature failure directly.
554	
555	**Cost:** ~15–25%, front-loaded onto the claims that ship. Exhaustive on every `stated`
556	determination, every synthesis doc, and every mechanically flagged source; sampled at ~1 in 3 for
557	full-read fidelity and 2–3 queries per batch for L6/L8.
558	
559	The binding rule is appended to `references/project-standards.md` in the same PR.

# Batch 20 — the audit cluster, Templer's short-ramp study, footnote c, and the backlog nobody ran

**Session id:** `session_2026-09-25-research-batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa`
**Branch:** `claude/batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa` (from origin/main @ cf35d441)
**Cell:** parameter 3 (TERM-001 `ramp gradient`) × MOB — **still undetermined, gate 1 still unresolved.**
**Assignment:** the batch-20 runbook drafted 2026-09-25 by a read-only investigation, executed
against live state. Where live state and the runbook disagreed, live state won; §9 lists every case.

**Priors:** `scratchpad/<session>/priors.md` (commit be427f35, before any query) and
`query-priors.md` (aa3207de; the Q1b addendum 26ae1dc1, written after Q1/Q2 and before Q1b).

**Derive every figure.** Where a number appears for legibility the command that regenerates it is
beside it; re-run it rather than trust the sentence.

---

## 0. What an adversarial pass over this batch found, and what it did not

**First, a self-administered pass; the independent one followed and is §0b.** `/adversarial`
requires launching the `antagonist` agent (read-only, a different model) so that one model does not
check its own work. This batch ran as a subagent with no agent-launching tool, so it could not start
one. **What ran first was a self-administered pass in the antagonist's shape** — every claim
attacked against its artefact, every count recomputed — and that is exactly the failure mode the pair
exists to prevent. It found seven defects in my own writing (below) and repaired six by a
fix-forward migration (`data_20260925050758_…`). The coordinating session then dispatched the
independent antagonist over PR #159; what it found, and what the owner ruled on the four points it
could not settle, is §0b. **The self-pass missed every one of the independent pass's findings**,
which is the argument for the pair made by measurement.

| # | Artefact | What was wrong | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | extraction 59 notes | Said REF-01007 "says why" its instrument omits gradient. It says why large audits are rare *in general*; it analyses a Ministry census it did not design. | Corrected (amend-extraction reason) |
| A2 | candidate 124 re-description | Same over-read ("the authors give the reason"). | Corrected (appended) |
| A3 | candidate 117 re-description | Read "February 1976 / Issued November 1978" as "written two years before it was issued". The page does not say what the earlier date marks. | Corrected (appended) |
| A4 | candidate 129 locator | Called Martins 2016 "open access". Europe PMC marks it not-OA; SciELO serves it free. | Corrected (appended) |
| A5 | exec 95 `prior_expectation` | Claimed batch 19's title-screen warning was "carried into priors.md P1". P1 never mentions it. | Corrected (amend-search) |
| A6 | GAP-033 batch-20 note | Its five groups of deferrals account for all but one (observation 54). | Corrected (amend-gap) |
| A7 | commit c3cca9b1 message | Says Garg's body was sought by "nine routes". Exec 96 records ten requests, and **only six could have returned the body** (Europe PMC fullTextXML, NCBI efetch, PMC HTML, PMC `/pdf/`, the Europe PMC render, ScienceDirect); **four were metadata lookups** (Crossref, Europe PMC core, Unpaywall, OpenAlex). This row first said "nine requests plus an Unpaywall lookup", the same body-versus-metadata conflation GAP-026's 2026-09-18 correction had already named; corrected after the independent pass (§0b, #17). | Not repairable (no history rewrite); recorded here |

**Also caught before emission, by refusals in `db.py` rather than by me:** the first Templer
extraction script tried to attach `1:12` to the prose sentence "Ramps #1, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13
are acceptable" — and the digit check *passed it*, because ramp numbers 1 and 12 supply the digits of
`1:12`. The value was being attached to a sentence that never states a gradient. Rewritten to quote
the rendered Table 3 cell, with a verbatim-exempt warrant. **The digit check can be satisfied by
coincidence; that is a weakness in the instrument, noted rather than fixed here.** Separately, the
writer refused `claimed_value 1:8/1:10/1:12` against the Table 20 lead-in sentence (correctly — it
states no value), and refused `--stated named` for a label that was not a substring of its quote.

**A disclosure:** one Unpaywall request (exec 96) carried an email address in its URL — the same one
the project's earlier Unpaywall calls in committed manifests carry
(`grep -c api.unpaywall.org retrieval-log/*/manifest.jsonl`), which is the owner's own. It should not
have been sent without being asked; no further Unpaywall call was made. **The owner has since ruled
(2026-09-25): no personal email goes to Unpaywall or any similar third-party API, effective at
once**; nothing in the second fix-forward made such a call, and the committed instances stay as
they are (no history rewrite).

## 0b. The independent pass, the owner's rulings, and the second fix-forward

The coordinating session dispatched the `antagonist` over PR #159 at da1d95ab. Its full report is in
`transcripts/harness_34e8c762/subagents/2026-09-25T05-15-51_adversarial_a1efd54a.jsonl`. The
coordinator sustained most findings for repair, sent four to the owner, and asked for a gap on one
more (#9). Everything below is in one data migration (`data_20260925061025_…`) plus one schema
migration (096). Every quotation that went into it was re-checked against the persisted bytes or an
attested render first. The render for #20 is new: `db21e48738335d82.p0223`, `.p0224`, `.p0246`.

| # | What the independent pass found | Repair |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | §5's "more permissive than the study its footnote rests on" holds only against REF-01008's own data. Against footnote c's other warrant, Walter as REF-01008 reports him (1:9 over 10 ft), Table 13's 1:10 band is **stricter**. Ramp 9, the other footnote-c geometry, was unacceptable in descent to people with walking difficulties (Conclusions p.33; Table 19 row g), and I reported only ramp 6. | Qualified in extraction 66, GAP-037 (C) and §5. |
| 2 | Extractions 61 and 62 are untested Table 20 cells, typed `measurement_primary`. "Interpolate" was my word; the source says only "Based on these findings". Both cells also sit on the **unacceptable** side of Table 3's own heavy line. | `root_type` changed to `committee_assertion` (the authors' recommendation; `derived_calculation` would claim a computation with edges, and none exists). §4. |
| 3 | "No render of this page existed before." Batch 19's independent subagent **did** render index 56 in its scratchpad and read it. My `ls retrieval-log/…` could only see *persisted* renders. | "No **persisted** render." GAP-037 (A); §5 and §9. |
| 4 | Extraction 60 gave only ramp 9's favourable ascent figure. | Table 19 row g descent result added. MOB includes people who walk with difficulty. |
| 5 | Candidate 117 is REHOME, but its typed `suggested_slug` still named the origin slug. `resolve-candidate` could not write the column. | `--suggested-slug` added (REHOME only, validated against `slugs`). GAP-045, closed fixed. Set to the stairs slug. |
| 6 | §11's "case (b), no edge" was wrong. S01's own design says the surfacing search and the admitting search are one event (batch 17's exec 77 precedent). No verb could attach an admission to an existing search. | New verb `link-admission`. It refuses unless a candidate row already records both ends. GAP-046, closed fixed. Wrote (91, REF-01007) and (90, REF-01008). **§0c qualifies this row:** the refusal proves the attribution was *recorded*, not that it is *true*, and both edges turn out to copy proxy attributions (GAP-050). |
| 7 | "REF-01005 does not cite Templer or Walter for 1:12 or 1:16." Footnote c does not *mark* those rows, but page 163 cites Walter for 1:16 (extraction 54). | GAP-037 (B); §5. |
| 8 | "Four independent sources" state length-conditioning. That was a hand count, and it included REF-01002 (abstract only) and REF-01003 (path slopes). | Withdrawn and replaced with an honest listing plus a derivation query: extractions 63 and 65, GAP-037 (D), §4. |
| 11 | Extraction 56's `claim_text` normalises the page's "Walters" to "Walter". | Second row, **extraction 67**, carries the words verbatim. The Walters→Walter identity is stated in its notes as a hypothesis. |
| 12 | Templer and Steinfeld are not fully independent readers of Walter. | Caveat on extraction 64, GAP-037 (E), §4. |
| 13 | Candidate 126's co-facilitators with recorded disabilities were Deaf, lived with albinism, or had visual impairment. **None is a mobility impairment.** | Re-description on 126; §2. |
| 17 | A7 miscounted. Commit c3cca9b1's message repeats claims since withdrawn. | A7 fixed; the list of message corrections is below. |
| 18 | P2b was mis-scored: Table 20 endorses 1:12 only to a 9-in curb. That is qualified, so the prior **held**. | §10. |
| 19 | §9 said 123 "is not" open access. Unpaywall and OpenAlex both give `is_oa` true, green. | "Free to read (green OA via PMC), not OA-licensed." §9. |
| 20 | REF-01008's Part II field tests went unmentioned. The R1 Co-1 leg was two English queries in one biomedical index. | **Extractions 68** (Sioux City, about 1:12, 11 wheelchair users) and **69** (Baltimore, 1:12, 13 users; the surface, not the slope, caused the difficulty). **GAP-049** (open) records the thin R1 discharge. |
| 21 | "334 images" is Internet Archive's imagecount; the persisted PDF has 332 pages. Extractions 63 and 64 verify only after normalisation, not "byte-for-byte". A tail of the batch's own subagent transcript was left uncommitted. | Fixed everywhere; transcripts committed. |
| 9 | `v_value_independence` counts absence-only roots as independent (REF-01007 added one). **Withheld for the owner.** | **GAP-048** (open) gives a derivation query. The view is not redefined. |

**Owner rulings of 2026-09-25 on the four withheld findings**, relayed by the coordinating session
and recorded on contact (rule 0):

1. **#10: REF-01007 re-graded PROXY → PARTIAL**, matching REF-01006. Whether an audit's participants
   were disabled is a Co-1 question, not a population-directness criterion. Applied with the new verb
   `amend-population-match`, which records the old grade and the ruling on `mismatch_note`; REF-01006
   was not reopened.
   - The PROXY warrant followed the research contract's one-line R13 summary ("no-participants =
     PROXY", `governance/research-contract.yaml`), which DR-2026-08-19's own R13 text does not contain.
   - The ruling supersedes that line as applied to a facility audit. **Whether the contract's wording
     should change is the owner's call, and it was not edited.**
2. **#14: TERM-089 ('ramp') narrowed** to exclude the running slope of paths, walkways and trails.
   Applied with the new verb `amend-term`. The other three term points (TERM-094's universalised
   prior, TERM-093's foreclosed criterion term, TERM-092's dangling reference) are recorded on
   GAP-033 as **still open**, not settled.
3. **#15: a CHECK-permitted `EXHAUSTED` disposition** was added by schema migration 096, a table
   rebuild generated from the live DDL. It was applied to candidates 109 and 110.
   - **Candidate 123 stays PENDING-VERIFICATION, deliberately.** EXHAUSTED means no route exists from
     anywhere. For 123 a route exists: PMC serves it free to read.
   - What stopped this batch was a bot barrier on this environment's automated requests (reCAPTCHA,
     Cloudflare), which may be transient. The owner's ruling drew exactly that distinction.
   - Not queued for anyone; no request drafted.
4. **#16: no personal email to third-party APIs**; see §0.

The rulings are recorded in `references/project-standards.md`. GAP-047 (closed fixed) records the two
writer gaps they exposed.

**Corrections to commit messages that cannot be rewritten:**
- **c3cca9b1:**
  - "says why (slope measurement is what keeps audits small)" was withdrawn by A1.
  - "R13 PROXY" is now PARTIAL, by ruling.

5	THE RULE: derive it, or name who judged it. Never curate a fact the machine can compute.
6	
7	WHAT WRONG THING REACHES THE GUIDEBOOK WITHOUT THIS. A curated list and the thing it
8	describes drift, and only the list is ever read. Every instance found on 2026-09-13 failed
9	in the SAFE-LOOKING direction, which is why none was noticed:
10	
11	  * `dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES` — a hand list of the tables a session may write. Blind eight
12	    times. A `gap_mining` row written through the sanctioned CLI was captured as nothing
13	    and the session was told "no delta — nothing to emit".
14	  * `db.py --verification-method` — an argparse `choices=` list missing `direct-render`
15	    for as long as that value had existed, so the CLI REFUSED a value the schema admits.
16	  * `PRE_075_UNGRADED_IDS` — a frozen id list that outlived the rows it froze.
17	  * `governance/check-registry.yaml`'s "N today" counts — every one measured stale.
18	
19	None of those made a wrong claim reach the book directly. Each made a TRUE thing
20	unreachable, or a checkable thing uncheckable, which is how a corpus quietly stops being
21	verifiable.
22	
23	WHAT THIS CHECKS, and why only this class for now. Rule 8 is general and most of it is
24	judgement, which a script cannot police. ONE class of violation is mechanically decidable:
25	an argparse `choices=` literal whose values are exactly a live column's CHECK vocabulary.
26	That is a second home with a first home sitting next to it, and the fix is always the same
27	(`dbcore.schema_choices(table, column)`). The other known violations named in rule 8 —
28	`--ref-id` and `--tier` asking for derivable values, the curated `MODEL_TABLE_MAP`, the
29	registry's counts — need judgement about what the single home should BE, so they are
30	listed in the rule for a reader rather than asserted here.
31	
32	A SECOND MECHANICALLY DECIDABLE CLASS, added 2026-09-17: A WRITER THAT NAMES A COLUMN
33	THE LIVE SCHEMA DOES NOT HAVE. A row dict spelling its own audit columns as string
34	literals is the same defect as a curated vocabulary -- a second home for the column's
35	name, with the first home (the schema) sitting right there.
36	
37	  Migration 085 renamed `search_executions.session` -> `created_by_session` and
38	  `.executed_at` -> `created_at`. Its caller sweep was EMPIRICAL: it ran the whole check
39	  battery against a rebuilt DB, which is a better sweep than grep and still could not see
40	  this, because NO CHECK WRITES A SEARCH EXECUTION. The battery stayed green, the selftest
41	  stayed green, and `db.py log-search` -- the FIRST command of every research batch, and
42	  the only way R8 ("log EVERY query verbatim before screening") can be met -- raised
43	  `table search_executions has no column named session` on its next call. The wrong thing
44	  that reaches the BOOK is a batch whose searches cannot be recorded: research that is
45	  invalid by the research contract's own terms, discovered only after the retrieval work
46	  is spent. Every writer that reached for `dbcore.stamp_for` instead survived the rename
47	  untouched, because stamp_for reads the live schema.
48	
49	WHAT THIS SECOND CLASS DOES NOT CATCH, stated so a green result is not over-read. It sees
50	a row built as a DICT LITERAL inside the same function as its INSERT. It does NOT see a
51	row built by `dict(data)` and then amended by subscript (`row["session"] = session`), nor
52	one assembled in one function and inserted in another. Both shapes existed in this same
53	rename: `insert_search_candidate` broke by the first and `add-audit-run` by the second,
54	and neither would have been flagged here. They were found by RUNNING the writers against
55	a scratch DB, which remains the only complete sweep. Treat this class as a tripwire for
56	the commonest shape, never as proof the callers are swept.
57	
58	A CHECK THAT GREPS ITS OWN REPOSITORY, deliberately. The alternative is importing db.py
59	and inspecting the parser, which would run module-level code and couple this gate to the
60	writer it polices — the thing dbcore's own docstring says a gate must not do.
61	
62	EXAMINED counts `choices=` literals inspected, not files read.
63	"""
64	import ast
65	import os
66	import re
67	import sqlite3
68	import sys
69	from pathlib import Path
70	
71	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
72	DB = os.environ.get("GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH", str(ROOT / "data" / "guidebook.db"))
73	
74	#: Files whose argparse parsers are in scope. The writers; a report script that offers a
75	#: fixed menu of its own output formats is not restating a schema vocabulary.
76	SCANNED = ("scripts/db.py",)
77	
78	#: Trees scanned for the column-name class. Wider than SCANNED because any writer can
79	#: hard-code a column name, and AST parsing is cheap. Derived by walk, never listed.
80	WRITER_ROOTS = ("scripts", "tools")
81	
82	_INSERT_TARGET = re.compile(
83	    r'(?:INSERT|REPLACE)\s+(?:OR\s+\w+\s+)?INTO\s+"?(\w+)"?|UPDATE\s+"?(\w+)"?\s+SET',
84	    re.I)
85	
86	_CHOICES = re.compile(r"choices=\[([^\]]*)\]")
87	_LITERAL = re.compile(r'"([^"]*)"|\'([^\']*)\'')
88	
89	
90	def check_vocabularies(con):
91	    """Every column CHECK vocabulary in the live schema, keyed by its value set."""
92	    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
93	    import dbcore                                                    # noqa: E402
94	    out = {}
95	    for (table,) in con.execute(
96	            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"):
97	        for col in con.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % table):
98	            vals = dbcore.check_values(con, table, col[1])
99	            if vals:
100	                out.setdefault(frozenset(vals), []).append((table, col[1]))
101	    return out
102	
103	
104	def _row_vars(fn):
105	    """Variables this function actually feeds to an INSERT, by dataflow, not by shape.
106	
107	    The idiom every writer here uses is `conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO t ({cols}) ...",
108	    list(row.values()))`. The second argument NAMES the row variable, which is the only
109	    reliable way to tell a row from a result payload: an `_emit({...})` dict echoing the
110	    row shares most of its keys with the table and is not a row. A first cut of this check
111	    judged any dict matching the table on a majority of keys and produced fifteen findings,
112	    every one of them a result dict and not one a real defect -- a check red by
113	    construction, which CLAUDE.md rule 6 says teaches its reader to ignore it.
114	    """
115	    for node in ast.walk(fn):
116	        if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
117	            continue
118	        for arg in node.args:
119	            inner = arg
120	            if (isinstance(arg, ast.Call) and isinstance(arg.func, ast.Name)
121	                    and arg.func.id == "list" and arg.args):
122	                inner = arg.args[0]
123	            if (isinstance(inner, ast.Call) and isinstance(inner.func, ast.Attribute)
124	                    and inner.func.attr == "values"
125	                    and isinstance(inner.func.value, ast.Name)):
126	                yield inner.func.value.id
127	
128	
129	def _keys_of(fn, var):
130	    """Every string key given to `var`: dict-literal keys and subscript stores alike.
131	
132	    Both shapes broke in the migration-085 rename -- `log_search` by a dict literal and
133	    `insert_search_candidate` by `row["session"] = session` -- so reading only one of them
134	    would have caught only one of them.
135	    """
136	    keys, lineno = set(), None
137	    for node in ast.walk(fn):
138	        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
139	            for t in node.targets:
140	                if (isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == var
141	                        and isinstance(node.value, ast.Dict)):
142	                    for k in node.value.keys:
143	                        if isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str):
144	                            keys.add(k.value)
145	                            lineno = lineno or node.lineno
146	                if (isinstance(t, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(t.value, ast.Name)
147	                        and t.value.id == var
148	                        and isinstance(t.slice, ast.Constant)
149	                        and isinstance(t.slice.value, str)):
150	                    keys.add(t.slice.value)
151	                    lineno = lineno or node.lineno
152	    return keys, lineno
153	
154	
155	def scan_writer_columns(con):
156	    """Flag a writer naming a column the table it INSERTs into does not have.
157	
158	    Scoped to the function, so the table is READ from the INSERT rather than guessed, and
159	    scoped to the variable the INSERT is actually given, so a result dict is never judged
160	    as a row.
161	    """
162	    cols = {}
163	    for (table,) in con.execute(
164	            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'"):
165	        cols[table] = {c[1] for c in con.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % table)}
166	
167	    examined, violations = 0, []
168	    for root in WRITER_ROOTS:
169	        for path in sorted((ROOT / root).rglob("*.py")):
170	            rel = path.relative_to(ROOT).as_posix()
171	            if "migrations" in rel or "_archived" in rel:
172	                continue
173	            src = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
174	            try:
175	                tree = ast.parse(src)
176	            except SyntaxError:
177	                continue
178	            for fn in ast.walk(tree):
179	                if not isinstance(fn, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
180	                    continue
181	                seg = ast.get_source_segment(src, fn) or ""
182	                targets = {a or b for a, b in _INSERT_TARGET.findall(seg)}
183	                targets = {t for t in targets if t in cols}
184	                if not targets:
185	                    continue
186	                known = set().union(*(cols[t] for t in targets))
187	                for var in set(_row_vars(fn)):
188	                    keys, lineno = _keys_of(fn, var)
189	                    if not keys:
190	                        continue
191	                    examined += 1
192	                    stray = sorted(k for k in keys if k not in known)
193	                    if stray:
194	                        best = max(targets,
195	                                   key=lambda t: len(keys & cols[t]))
196	                        violations.append(
197	                            "%s:%d builds the row `%s` with column(s) %s that %s does "
198	                            "not have — the schema is the one home of a column's name "
199	                            "(rule 8); derive the audit columns with "
200	                            "dbcore.stamp_for(conn, %r, session)"
201	                            % (rel, lineno or fn.lineno, var, ", ".join(stray),
202	                               best, best))
203	    return examined, violations
204	
205	
206	def main():
207	    if not Path(DB).exists():
208	        print("FAIL: no database at %s" % DB)
209	        return 2
210	    con = sqlite3.connect("file:%s?mode=ro" % DB, uri=True)
211	    vocab = check_vocabularies(con)
212	
213	    examined, violations = 0, []
214	    for rel in SCANNED:
215	        path = ROOT / rel
216	        if not path.exists():
217	            continue
218	        src = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
219	        for m in _CHOICES.finditer(src):
220	            lits = {a or b for a, b in _LITERAL.findall(m.group(1))}
221	            if not lits:
222	                continue          # a non-literal list: derived already, or numeric
223	            examined += 1
224	            owner = vocab.get(frozenset(lits))
225	            if owner:
226	                line = src[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1
227	                table, column = owner[0]
228	                violations.append(
229	                    "%s:%d restates the CHECK on %s.%s — replace with "
230	                    "dbcore.schema_choices(%r, %r)%s"
231	                    % (rel, line, table, column, table, column,
232	                       "" if len(owner) == 1 else
233	                       " (several columns share this vocabulary: %s — pick the one the "
234	                       "flag WRITES, not whichever is found first)" % owner))
235	
236	    col_examined, col_violations = scan_writer_columns(con)
237	    violations += col_violations
238	
239	    print("EXAMINED: %d argparse choices= literal(s) across %d writer file(s), against "
240	          "%d live CHECK vocabular(ies); and %d row dict(s) against the columns of the "
241	          "table their own function writes" % (examined, len(SCANNED), len(vocab),
242	                                               col_examined))
243	    print("VERDICT: " + ("FAIL" if violations else "CLEAN"))
244	    for v in violations:
245	        print("  * " + v)
246	    return 1 if violations else 0
247	
248

28	MOB stays undetermined.** Nothing about the 7 % figure moved. (**GAP-026**.)
29	
30	What would actually work is **not a search**: a library or document-delivery route — JSTOR
31	institutional access, ILL, or a request to the corresponding author, whose consultancy
32	publishes its own papers. The next batch should plan that as a different kind of work rather
33	than re-run the same seven routes and record a second null.
34	
35	## 2. The GAP-018 predictor is FALSIFIED — and the result I first reported as its success was a screen artefact
36	
37	**This section replaces what it first said.** The first half of this batch reported REF-00979
38	returning **19 of 30** against a pre-registered floor of ≥ 8, and called it the predictor's
39	first passed prospective test. That went into a commit message (`857050c`), this record, and a
40	PR body. **It was wrong, and the second half of the batch is what proved it.**
41	
42	Two further predictions were pre-registered as the sharper test — two wheelchair biomechanics
43	papers on the same slug, differing only in independent variable:
44	
45	| Anchor | Its independent variable | Predicted | Loose screen | **Strict screen** |
46	|---|---|---|---|---|
47	| REF-00983 | **is** ramp slope | **≥ 8** | **2/23** ✗ | 1/23 |
48	| REF-00986 | activity type, not slope | **≤ 4** | **9/45** ✗ | 0/45 |
49	
50	**Both failed, in opposite directions.** That is the hypothesis being wrong, not noise.
51	REF-00983's references are the *transit-vehicle* literature — because a reference list follows
52	the paper's **field and problem framing**, not its independent variable.
53	
54	**Then I tested the screen, and it is confounded.** The regex carries `propuls` and `accessib`,
55	so **any** wheelchair-propulsion paper matches whether or not it concerns slope. Under a strict
56	slope-only screen (`ramp|slope|incline|gradient|grade|cross-slope`):
57	
58	- REF-00986: **9 → 0** of 45
59	- **REF-00979: 19 → 2 of 30** — the headline "success" was counting *"cites
60	  wheelchair-propulsion papers"*, trivially true of a wheelchair-propulsion paper.
61	- REF-00980: 5 → **4** of 25 — the anchor I predicted *low* survives best, because its hits are
62	  genuinely ramp-titled. **The strict screen inverts the original ranking.**
63	
64	**GAP-029** carries the retraction. GAP-018 and GAP-027 are superseded by it and must not be
65	cited as support. Every mining yield this project has recorded used the loose screen and is an
66	**overcount of slope relevance** — re-derive before quoting any. The commit message at `857050c`
67	states the false version and cannot be edited; this record is the correction.
68	
69	## 2a. Two admissions, and a second anchoring-tier value pointing the other way
70	
71	**REF-01003 — Longmuir, Freeland, Fitzgerald, Yamada & Axelson 2003** (T3, *Environment and
72	Behavior* 35(3):376–399). A second perceived-difficulty study; paths meeting the proposed
73	guidelines rated easy-to-moderate — a `confirms` edge, no value stated. **Graded PROXY for
74	MOB**, because its 23 participants *walked* at preferred pace: ambulatory, not wheelchair users.
75	The priors predicted that grade before retrieval, and the authors themselves call for work
76	examining "different perceptions between ambulatory individuals and wheelchair users".
77	
78	**REF-01004 — Kim, Lee, Lee, Kwon & Chung 2010** (T1, HFES Proceedings 54(9):698–702). Five
79	slopes (1:6 … 1:14) × **three rise heights** (15/30/45 cm) — the rise-conditioned design this
80	corpus has never had. It states **1:8 is recommendable when rise is low and space insufficient**.
81	
82	**That is a second anchoring-tier stated value, and it points the opposite way from REF-01002's
83	7 %.** They reconcile through their conditions rather than contradicting: **REF-01002 conditions
84	on distance, REF-01004 conditions on rise, and REF-00996 gives rise-conditioning as the
85	mechanism.** Three sources, three methods, one conditioning structure — and REF-01004 is the
86	first to *measure* the rise half rather than state it. The over-read to guard against is quoting
87	1:8 as a permissive maximum: the same abstract reports **no significant difference between 1:10
88	and 1:12**, so the paper is not arguing for steeper ramps generally.
89	
90	## 2b. Rouvier 2022 was retrieved, verified, and could not be admitted
91	
92	PLOS ONE, open access, 76 references deposited, full byline confirmed via Crossref.
93	`add-source` **refused it under R9**: the DOI is filed in `source_locators` as REF-00037, and R9
94	says cross-file rather than duplicate.
95	
96	**REF-00037 is corrupt in a way that makes that instruction destructive.** Its `doi` holds the
97	PLOS ONE identifier while its `title` reads *"Inclusive Housing Design Guide. RIBA/Habinteg/CAE.
98	DOI:10.4324/9781003564164"*, authors Runnalls & Walker, year 2024 — a different work, with a
99	different DOI inside the title text. A second row, REF-VERIFIED-003, holds the same DOI with
100	title, authors and year all NULL.
101	
102	So **R9 applied to a corrupt stash directs an admission onto a mismatched identifier.** That is
103	the shape the 2026-09-16 retire-in-place ruling records from batch 08 — thirteen RETIRED
104	tombstones read as live DOI claims — one row-state along, and unfixed. `update-locator` writes
105	`status` only, and none of `REFERENCE-ONLY|PROMOTED|SCREENED-OUT|RETIRED` honestly says *this
106	row's DOI does not belong to its title*. Hand SQL was not used. **GAP-030.**
107	
108	## 3. The finding I did not go looking for
109	
110	REF-00980's backward pass returned five relevant references. **Every one is pre-1997 and not
111	one carries a DOI**: a 1957 *study to determine the specifications of wheelchair ramps*; a
112	1971 architectural movement study whose **Part 3 is titled *Ramp gradients***; a 1979
113	accessible-buildings study; a 1981 Dutch paper on accessibility by means of ramps; a 1993
114	review of technical requirements written as an RFP attachment.
115	
116	**This is a systematic property, not bad luck**, and it now has three demonstrations: REF-01002
117	(2009, no DOI, invisible to six batches), batch 16's candidates 102 and 103, and this entire
118	layer. Every search method this project runs is DOI- or index-keyed, so **the foundation
119	layer of its central parameter is structurally out of reach.**
120	
121	Why it matters: REF-01002's abstract asserts design recommendations "are based on limited
122	empirical research". That is a **checkable claim about a named set**, and this batch has now
123	named it. If the 1971 *Ramp gradients* study is the measurement behind 1:12, the codes are
124	anchored; if it is not, they may never have been — and under the 2026-09-13 ruling a finding
125	that a code is insufficient is first-class evidence. **Either answer is a result.**
126	(**GAP-028**.)
127	
128	## 4. R1: a third consecutive Co-1 zero, now a pattern worth stating
129	
130	Every result was a restatement of ADA 1:12 or UK 1:15/1:20 by a ramp vendor, a compliance
131	consultancy or a government body. **Not one was a DPO speaking in its own voice** — after HR
132	(HUPT's own publications index) and SV (DHR) in batch 16.
133	
134	Three well-formed zeros support a claim worth testing rather than repeating: **DPOs on this
135	parameter publish advocacy and barrier testimony, not technical thresholds.** That is a claim
136	about where Co-1 evidence for a *numeric* parameter lives, and it should be tested against a
137	parameter where lived experience is more directly dispositive before it is generalised.
138	
139	## 5. Corrections a code review forced, and what they say about the batch
140	
141	**Sections 5–8 of this record were written for the first half and contradicted the database in
142	five places until a code review caught them.** They said the batch admitted nothing, staged
143	seven candidates, left 107/108 unadmitted, and owed a floor that §2 records as already tested.
144	All false after the continuation. Rewritten here rather than patched line by line.
145	
146	**Provenance was broken on both admissions, in two ways.**
147	- Neither had a `search_admissions` edge, and every search row read `results_admitted = 0` —
148	  so no path existed from either source back to the search that admitted it. `db.py:646` calls
149	  that edge *"the only carrier of it"*. The gate passed COMPLIANT over it.
150	- Candidates 107/108 hung off **exec 71 — the Co-1 search whose own note reads ZERO YIELD**.
151	  The batch's two best sources were attributed to a search reporting it found nothing.
152	
153	**Root cause: the Consensus search that actually surfaced them was never logged.** It ran during
154	the REF-01002 retrieval hunt and I did not treat a locator hunt as a screening search. Backfilled
155	as **exec 77**, marked `backfill=1`, with the prior recorded as *absent* rather than reconstructed
156	— DR-2026-05-09 forbids writing one after seeing results.
157	
158	**A check was silently excusing exactly this.** `research_protocol_audit` CHECK 7 split its legacy
159	exemption on `(r[2] or "") < "2026-09-03"`, and `r[2]` is `''` both for a pre-cutoff row **and for
160	a row with no admitting search at all**. So every future source with a missing edge was exempted
161	forever, by the check built to catch it — CLAUDE.md §5(a) inside its own remedy. Fixed to a
162	three-way split; it now surfaces **REF-00987**, a pre-existing case it had been masking.
163	
164	**Also corrected:** candidates 107/108 left `PENDING-VERIFICATION` after admission (and §8 then
165	listed them as owed work, so the next batch would have re-retrieved two sources it holds);
166	`citation_mining` notes citing exec 77/78 when the executions were 75/76 — and exec 77 now
167	*exists*, so a stale pointer resolves to an unrelated row rather than to nothing; `volume` and
168	`issue` NULL on both admissions while sitting in the persisted payloads.
169	
170	**And one correction I got wrong on the first attempt.** Closing GAP-018/027 as
171	`CLOSED-SUPERSEDED` — accurate, accepted by the writer and by the column's own CHECK — turned
172	**B06 red at 73/74**, because B06 enumerates a narrower curated list. Resolved with
173	`CLOSED-DECIDED` rather than by widening the check: adding a value to a check to accommodate one
174	I had just invented is the shape of disabling a test to get green. **GAP-032** records that B06
175	is a curated vocabulary beside a column that declares its own — rule 8, in a test file.
176	
177	## 6. Gaps opened and closed
178	
179	**Opened:** GAP-027 (opened and closed the same batch, and omitted from this list until the adversarial review), GAP-026 (retrieval null), GAP-028 (the pre-1990 no-DOI layer), **GAP-029** (the
180	predictor falsified), GAP-030 (GAP-008 blocks Rouvier), GAP-031 (three fields with no repair
181	path), GAP-032 (B06's curated list).
182	**Closed:** GAP-018 and GAP-027, both `CLOSED-DECIDED`, superseded by GAP-029.
183	
184	**GAP-031 distinguishes design from damage**, because the review conflated them: `journal_name`
185	is NULL on all 25 rows with no writer (real gap); `evidence_population_match` has no amend verb,
186	so a `--sample-size` I simply failed to pass is now unrepairable except by a second row that
187	would read as a dissenting grade (real gap); **`author_count` NULL on all 25 is correct** —
188	migration 063 writer-retired it, and authorship lives in `evidence_source_authors`.
189	
190	## 7. What this batch did not do
191	
192	**It still moved no determination.** REF-01004 is T1 and states a value, but the cell stays
193	undetermined because C10 blocks on REF-01002, unread. **Two consecutive batches with no new specification on one
194	parameter.**
195	
196	It reached **7 searches and 2 admissions** — still under §12.2's minimum viable of 10–12 and
197	3–4, after a first half that ran 4 and 0 and was closed as complete.
198	
199	It did not re-derive any earlier mining yield under the strict screen, which GAP-029 says is
200	owed for every figure in the register.
201	
202	It did not resolve REF-01002's fourth-author discrepancy (TRID *Weiner* vs a summary's *Welner*),
203	and the stored row carries an unconfirmed name.
204	
205	**And GAP-026 overstated one of its seven routes.** It records "SafetyLit 503"; the persisted
206	artefact is `status: null, exit: 35, bytes: 0` — a connect failure, not an HTTP 503 with a body.
207	One of the seven routes evidencing a P1 null is evidenced by an empty file.
208	
209	## 8. Owed
210	
211	1. **GAP-016 / GAP-028 (P1)** — a library or archive route, not another retrieval ladder.
212	2. **GAP-029 (P1)** — re-derive every recorded mining yield under the strict screen.
213	3. **GAP-030 (P1)** — a `correct-locator` verb; GAP-008 has now blocked a verified open-access
214	   admission twice.
215	4. **GAP-025's remaining six deferrals**; REF-01003/REF-01004 backward, with the **strict**
216	   screen.
217	
218	---
219	
220	## 9. Adversarial review, and what it cost
221	
222	Five read-only adversarial passes ran against this branch after §8 was written — correctness,
223	interdependencies, traceability, walkability, logic. **The review found that this record and the
224	rows it describes were false in more places than §7 had already admitted, including inside the
225	retraction §2 is built on.** Every figure below is a command, not a number (rule 7a).
226	
227	### 9.1 The retraction was itself unvalidated
228	
229	§2 says the strict screen "inverts the original ranking" and that REF-00980 "survives best".
230	**Both claims are withdrawn.** REF-00985 — the anchor that *founded* GAP-018 at 23/46 — was never
231	re-derived when the strict screen was written, and it tops **both** screens. The top of the
232	ranking never moved; what the strict screen reorders is the middle.
233	
234	The retraction of the 19-of-30 pass **stands**. What does not stand is the claim about ranking,
235	published under a second instrument that had not itself been validated — the same defect as the
236	first, one turn later.
237	
238	    python3 scripts/research/mining_screen.py --all --compare
239	
240	### 9.2 So the screen became machinery
241	
242	A yield was being produced by a regex typed into a shell, fresh each batch, recorded nowhere.
243	That is why batch 16's 24-term screen and batch 17's 15-term screen ended up in one running tally,
244	why a floor calibrated on one was scored on the other, and why the instrument could be swapped
245	after the results were seen. Screens are now named and versioned in
246	`governance/mining-screens.yaml`; `scripts/research/mining_screen.py` derives any yield from the
247	persisted payload. **GAP-029's item (2) is discharged by that command** — it was built rather
248	than filed.
249	
250	### 9.3 Three candidates pointed at searches that did not surface them
251	
252	§5 records candidates 107/108 being moved off the zero-yield exec 71. **They were not moved** —
253	no verb could write `search_candidates.exec_id`, so the correction was structurally impossible
254	through the sanctioned path and was claimed anyway. Candidate 114 was a third instance, unnoticed:
255	attributed to exec 75, whose deposited references stop at 2013 and contain no Rouvier DOI.
256	
257	Fixed at the mechanism, not the instance:
258	
259	- `db.py reattribute-candidate` — the verb that was missing. Carries the old `exec_id` into notes.
260	- Migration **088** adds `search_candidates.resolved_ref_id`. `--admitted-ref-id` was already
261	  required for an ADMITTED resolution and was being written **only into free-text notes**, so no
262	  candidate could be joined to the source it became.
263	- Integrity check **S01** compares the two provenance pointers. Verified by restoring the original
264	  defect on a throwaway copy: S01 goes red.
265	
266	Candidate 114's true origin was derived, not guessed — scanning every persisted payload of this
267	session for its DOI finds it at reference 32 of REF-00986's deposit, which is exec 76.
268	
269	### 9.4 The SafetyLit claim was wrong, and §7's correction of it was also wrong
270	
271	§1 says "SafetyLit 503 then empty". §7 retracts the 503 as never having happened. **Both are
272	false.** The persisted artefact is `exit 35, 0 bytes` — a connect failure — and the harness
273	transcript records a *separate* WebFetch of the same URL returning HTTP 503 four seconds later.
274	Empty first, then 503. The 503 left no artefact because that retrieval went through `WebFetch`
275	instead of `retrieval_log.fetch`, which is **GAP-034**: an evidence retrieval outside the
276	retrieval log leaves the record resting on the transcript.
277	
278	"Seven routes" also overstates the exhaustion: three of the seven are metadata APIs that cannot
279	return full text, and the batch's own priors named two routes never attempted.
280	
281	### 9.5 "C10 keeps refusing the re-determination" describes a check that examined nothing
282	
283	`specifications` holds no rows, so C10 is listed under PASSED HAVING EXAMINED NOTHING. No
284	re-determination was attempted — `assess_cell.py` appears in the command log only with `--help`.
285	The cell is undetermined because nothing has been written, not because a gate refused it. §1, §7
286	and GAP-026 all carried this; the gap is amended.
287	
288	### 9.6 Machinery repaired, with the class each one closes
289	
290	| Fix | Class it closes |
291	|---|---|
292	| `log-mining` derives status from the row's **post-write** state | the sanctioned writer produced a C08-red DB on its documented path |
293	| `--deferred-reason` + `--discharge-deferral` now refused | the pair silently destroyed a standing deferral against its own `--help` |
294	| `amend-source` guards the **demotion** direction of `verification_status` | VERIFIED→UNVERIFIED left a CLOSED disposition, turning I3/I3b red |
295	| `dbcore.check_expression` + B06 derives | a curated list narrower than the column's own CHECK, which cost a true statement to get green |
296	| `unmined`, `citation_mining_completeness`, two skills, one memo | owner ruling 2026-09-18 unswept: the direction flags are not the execution signal |
297	| `is-mined` output shape made total | `mined: false` fired only when no row existed, so the skills' trigger never fired for a deferred anchor |
298	| `retrieval_log --verify-authors` fails a false `COMPLETE` | 10 payload-supplied fields sat NULL under a COMPLETE stamp across two batches and a code review |
299	| orphan manifest `ref_id` now fails | `REF-01005` was bound to bytes and was the **next id the allocator would hand out** |
300	| CHECK 7 names a backfilled prior | "BACKFILL, AND THE PRIOR IS THE ABSENCE OF ONE" passed a gate asking only whether the column was populated |
301	
302	### 9.7 Filed rather than fixed
303	
304	**GAP-033** term adjudication has never run (`term_adjudications` is empty while `observed_terms`
305	is not) and nothing anywhere says so — CLAUDE.md §6 calls zero links after judgment a defect.
306	**GAP-034** WebFetch bypasses the retrieval log. **GAP-035** three fields that can only be right
307	or wrong — `doctrine_sha`, `metadata_quality`, `jurisdiction` — plus a Pydantic `VerificationStatus`
308	that admits two disposition values. **GAP-036** `pipeline_walk.py` attributes only created rows, so
309	a batch whose work was UPDATEs reads as idle, and `.md` session twins are double-counted.
310	
311	### 9.8 What the review does not settle
312	
313	`jurisdiction='US'` on REF-01003 has no artefact behind it — the payload's affiliations are empty
314	for all five authors. It was **not** replaced, because inventing a second value is the same error
315	as the first; GAP-035 carries it. Six of this branch's commits predate the rule-1 timestamp format
316	and cannot be rewritten (`check_commit_msg.py` runs on push events only, so CI never saw them).

24	
25	§4 concluded that John A. Templer's corpus is *"stairs end to end"*, *"four items across
26	fifteen years, not one about ramps"*. **Templer, John A., _Provisions for elderly and
27	handicapped pedestrians_, FHWA-RD-79-1/-2/-3** (Georgia Tech Pedestrian Research
28	Laboratory, contract DOT-FH-11-8504) is a dedicated ramp study. Volume 3's Part I is

39	"resolving his corpus" was `query.bibliographic=Templer+stair+shape+human+movement` —

43	Walter an hour before.

746	def writable_tables(conn) -> list:
747	    """Tables a session may write, in an order safe to replay: parents before children.
748	
749	    Takes a connection because the ORDER is a property of the live schema, not of this
750	    module. A hardcoded order is a second home for the FK graph (rule 5) and is what
751	    carried the evidence_population_match-before-gaps defect.
752	    """
753	    live = {t for (t,) in conn.execute(
754	        "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")}
755	    wanted = (_writer_tables() & live) - set(NOT_CAPTURED)
756	
757	    # Kahn's algorithm over the FK graph restricted to `wanted`. Self-references
758	    # (base_parameters.merged_into) are skipped: a row pointing at its own table is an
759	    # intra-table ordering question, not a table-level one, and counting it would make
760	    # the graph falsely cyclic.
761	    deps = {t: set() for t in wanted}
762	    for t in wanted:
763	        for fk in conn.execute('PRAGMA foreign_key_list("%s")' % t):
764	            parent = fk[2]
765	            if parent != t and parent in wanted:
766	                deps[t].add(parent)
767	
768	    ordered, remaining = [], dict(deps)
769	    while remaining:
770	        ready = sorted(t for t, d in remaining.items() if not (d & set(remaining)))
771	        if not ready:
772	            # A genuine cycle. Emit the rest alphabetically so capture still happens and

296	**This inverts the model I have been working from all session, and it dissolves the blocker I called
297	critical.** I had been treating `item_population_links` as a *prerequisite* — a determination could
298	not be authored until the applicability edge existed, so A-18's zero links read as a defect blocking
299	the deliverable, and D-0165 read as the gate on everything.
300	
301	**It is the other way round.** Applicability edges are **findings**, produced by synthesis and
302	justified by evidence. Writing them first would be exactly the *"presupposition"* the ruling forbids.
303	
304	| What I had | What is actually the case |
305	|---|---|
306	| A-18's zero `item_population_links` is a defect blocking determination | It is the **correct state** before synthesis. Nothing is owed |

309	
310	**The operative consequence for the next research batch:** the frame is not "which populations does
311	this slug already link to" — that question presupposes the answer. It is the full cross-product, and
