# Diagnostic survey: why the same defect shapes recur in the Guidebook's research pipeline

**Scope and method.** Read-only, 2026-09-26. Base is worktree HEAD `cf35d441` (main); the batch-20 specimen lives on branch `claude/batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa` (head `4f41b11b`), which I read via `git show`. The harness refused every `git show | python3` pipe, so I could not open the branch's DB; GAP-045..052 were read from the branch's data-migration SQL (`scripts/migrations/data_2026092[56]*.sql`), which is the only route rows take into the DB. Live counts below are from HEAD's `data/guidebook.db` opened `mode=ro`, or from `grep`/AST over HEAD's code. Every figure is measured today and will drift; the command is named where it matters. I read CLAUDE.md, DR-2026-08-19 (all 1,009 lines), the batch-20 record in full, batch records 06, 07, 10, 13, 17, 19 in full and 08, 09, 14, 15, 16, 18 in their self-review sections, the ledger tail (`references/project-standards.md` ~3560–3962 plus the 2026-09-11 entries), the check registry, `test_db_integrity.py` S01/H05, `derived_not_curated_audit.py`, `dbcore.writable_tables`, the `/adversarial`, `/batch-done` commands, the `antagonist` agent, and `.claude/settings.json` hooks.

---

## 1. The specimen, compressed to what it proves

Batch 20 (`sessions/session_2026-09-25-research-batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa.md`, branch only) went through three review rounds in ~24 hours:

- **Round 0 (self-pass, §0):** 7 defects found, 6 repaired. The self-pass "missed every one of the independent pass's findings."
- **Round 1 (independent antagonist, §0b):** 21 findings, including the headline "Table 13's band is more permissive than the study its footnote rests on" (true against one warrant, false against the other), "four independent sources" (a hand count including an abstract and a path-slope study), "no render of this page existed before" (false: batch 19's subagent rendered it and did not persist it). Also: the author's own pre-write quote checks tested a `(found, detail)` tuple's truth — vacuous for the whole batch.
- **Round 2 (code review, §0c):** the verb written in round 1 to satisfy S01 (`link-admission`) copies the very column S01 compares, so S01 cannot fail on anything it writes; the `--suggested-slug` fix was optional and existence-only; `amend-term` nested audit lines and skipped the `fk_declared`/`check_declared` gates its siblings apply; zero tests covered any new refusal; and `link-admission`'s `results_admitted` sync reintroduced a mechanism the 2026-09-02 repair had deliberately retired (H05). Verifying S01's edges then showed both copy proxy attributions: Pinto came from a reference list, Templer from an Internet Archive lookup during batch 19's adversarial pass — neither a logged search (GAP-050).

One document therefore contains: self-review that misses what a fresh reader catches; a repair that is tautological against the check it satisfies; a curated-gate omission in a sibling writer; a doctrine collision invisible to the author; a provenance model that cannot represent how two sources were actually found; and four review agents converging three times on one duplicated block.

---

## 2. Answers to the seven structural questions

### Q1. Self-validating checks — a class, not a one-off

S01 (`scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py:293–342`) compares `search_candidates.exec_id` with `search_admissions.exec_id`. `link_admission` (branch, `scripts/db.py`) refuses unless a candidate row records both ends, then writes that candidate's `exec_id` as the admission's `exec_id`. Agreement is manufactured by construction. S01's own comment already says the shape is "CLAUDE.md rule 5's shape — one fact with two homes"; it chose to police the dual home rather than remove it, and a verb closed the loop seven days later.

The same shape, on the record, before batch 20:

- **H05** (deleted 2026-09-02; comment at `test_db_integrity.py:1082–1095`): parity between `results_admitted` and `search_admissions`. "The gate did not detect drift; it CAUSED a research-stage record to be rewritten so the second home would agree with the first" — seven searches' counts set to 0 on 2026-09-01.
- **H01/H02** (deleted 2026-09-21, comment at `:1050–1056`): "the engine wrote the JSON copy SO THAT this check would pass, and assess_cell said so in its own comment."
- **H03/H04** (deleted 2026-08-24): same reason.
- **`research_protocol_audit` CHECK 7** (batch 17 §5): split its legacy exemption on `(r[2] or "") < "2026-09-03"`, and `''` is both a pre-cutoff row and a row with no admitting search — "every future source with a missing edge was exempted forever, by the check built to catch it."
- **`citation_mining_completeness`** (batch 16 §5b; ledger 2026-09-18): counts row presence, reporting "10/10 T1-2 sources mined, 100.0%" while 3 of 13 backward passes had run — the writer `log_mining` set `backward=1` unconditionally, including on deferrals.
- **Batch 09** (`session_2026-09-16-research-batch-09-…md:107–133`): `normalise_quote` reduced text to `[^0-9a-z]`, so an invented Japanese sentence "verified against the artefact." The anti-fabrication control was vacuous for six of nineteen languages.
- **Batch 20 §0**: the digit check accepted `1:12` against a sentence listing ramps "1, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12" — satisfied by coincidence.
- **2026-08-19** (CLAUDE.md §5c): six gates passed fabricated co-authors "because each asked whether the author fields were populated, never whether they were true."

Would a registry review have caught S01? There is no such review. S01 is one of 62 `record()` ids under a single registry entry (`governance/check-registry.yaml:254`, `test_db_integrity`, `min_items: 1` for the whole battery). `run_checks.py --selftest` C1–C9 (`scripts/run_checks.py:666–815`) test registry coherence (unique ids, batteries declared, executables exist, classification, selection). Nothing anywhere reviews a check's logic against the writer whose output it examines. New db.py writers have landed in fix-forward commits inside research PRs in batches 15, 17, 19 and 20, and each was found defective by the next optional review (batch 15 §10: `link-source-slug` "collected the adjudication and recorded it never"; batch 19 §14: `journal_name` added to `_CORRECTABLE` broke the invariant in that constant's own header; batch 20 §0c above).

### Q2. Curated-list drift — the derived path is opt-in and blind at write time

Measured on HEAD (`scripts/db.py`): 51 `choices=` lists, 25 derived via `dbcore.schema_choices/check_values`, 26 literal. Of 46 writer-like functions (`def insert_|add_|log_|amend_|link_|resolve_|correct_|…`), 15 call `stamp_for`, 8 call `check_declared`/`check_values`, **2** call `fk_declared` (`amend_source`, `amend_extraction`), and 26 call none of the three. Still-curated module lists: `_AMENDABLE` (:3875), `_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS` (:6258), `_COVERAGE_COLS`, `_BPC_META_COLS`, `_VALID_DIRECTIONS`, `_VALID_CONFLICT_STATUS`, `_VALID_ITEM_STATUS`, `_VALID_RUN_STATUS`, `_PIPELINE_STEPS`, `_SVE_VOCAB_COLUMNS`. GAP-042 records four `evidence_sources` vocabularies that live only in a test file. GAP-013 records the `_AMENDABLE` inversion deferred because it was "a change to make deliberately, not at the end of a long session" (batch 19 §15).

Why it recurs, specifically:

1. **`derived_not_curated_audit.py`** (blocking) is proactive only for two shapes: an argparse `choices=` literal whose value set exactly equals a live CHECK, and a dict-literal row key absent from the schema. Its docstring (lines 49–56) states it cannot see `dict(data)`+subscript rows, cross-function assembly, or — the shape that recurred in batch 20 — a new writer omitting the gates its siblings apply. Nothing lints sibling asymmetry: `relate-extraction` lacked the `--verbatim-exempt` that `add-extraction` has (GAP-007, batch 13); `amend-search` could not record a late admission that `log-search` could (batch 09 §"Tooling defects"); `log-mining` could not express "ran and found nothing" (batch 16 §5); `amend_term` lacked `fk_declared`/`check_declared` (batch 20).
2. **A literal is invisible until the column declares a CHECK.** `check_declared` is a no-op on an unconstrained column, so "derived" silently degrades to unguarded (batch 19 §10a: `add-source --source-type` "accepted the bad value … because an undeclared vocabulary reads as no constraint"). The audit "went red in the same run" only when migration 091 added a CHECK (batch 19 §15) — proving the detector fires after the fact, on the schema change, not on the literal.
3. **The comment does not protect the reader.** WRITABLE_TABLES' eighth blindness "was added by the author who was reading those comments at the time" (CLAUDE.md rule 8); B05's curated tuple sat "eleven lines below" the comment recording B06's fix of the identical pattern (batch 19 §10a); rule 7a's stale count sits inside rule 7a; batch 19 records "rule 7a on its third outing in this batch."

### Q3. Doctrine currency — five stores, no index, annotation by habit

There is no "what is current" index. CLAUDE.md §9 points at DR-2026-08-19 for "what to do now" and the ledger tail for "latest rulings"; rule 0 says live rulings override on contact and §7 says "Owner rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`," which `.ignore` hides from the Grep tool. Doctrine therefore lives in: DRs (write-once, annotated when someone remembers), the ledger (append-only; rulings correct earlier rulings and, per the 2026-09-18 entry, their own snippets), CLAUDE.md (edited in place, history in git), code comments (GAP-051 cites "the H05 comment in `scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py`" as the record of the retirement), and session records (hidden from ripgrep). Correctness depends on which subset a session reads.

Unannotated supersessions I could confirm:

- **DR-2026-08-24 §2.4** ("Applicability is an OUTPUT of synthesis"): CLAUDE.md §6 says the owner overruled it on 2026-08-27. The DR carries a 2026-08-25 superseded-notice on a *different* section (line 229) and nothing on §2.4 (lines 285–312).
- **DR-2026-07-22-work-from-axes**: `axes` was ruled "a bad coined term … do not relitigate" on 2026-08-18 (CLAUDE.md rule 0 proof). Zero annotation in the DR.
- **DR-2026-05-09-adversarial-research-protocol**: "Supersedes: None"; DR-2026-08-19 §7 "repointed" adversarial review. Zero annotation.
- **DR-2026-08-19 step 7** ("in one transaction: UPDATE search_executions SET … results_admitted") vs the 2026-09-02 H05 retirement: the repair session (`sessions/session_2026-09-02-owed-repairs.md:47`) never cites the DR; the collision was found 24 days later by a code review, and the DR was not annotated even then (GAP-051 instead).
- **`governance/research-contract.yaml:229–231`** ("no-participants = PROXY") vs DR-2026-08-19's R13 text: found 2026-09-25; the ruling supersedes it "as applied", and the line was deliberately left in place.
- **D-0170 vs D-0184** (ledger 2026-09-11): "A session reading D-0170 alone would have built the wrong thing, correctly citing a ratified DR while doing it."
- **DR-2026-08-19 §1.5** already documents this for DR-2026-08-06 §3: "That reasoning no longer holds, and the DR was never annotated."

Census: 83 DRs, 33 contain any supersession/amendment wording (`grep -il 'superseded by|overruled|AMENDED 20|STRUCK 20|CORRECTION' decisions/DR-*.md`). The operative instrument itself — written to end the "re-derive, re-litigate, re-render" recursion its §0 measured at ~30% of commits — has been amended in place at least six times (08-22, 08-23, 08-25, 09-02, 09-10, 09-26), and its §12.1 is "SUPERSEDED 2026-09-10 — see `workplan/2026-09-10-batch-06-runbook.md`," a fifth document its §8 says may not exist.

### Q4. Why self-review fails the same way, and where the adversarial pass sits

**The shape of what self-review misses** is consistent across batches 17, 19 and 20:

- *The more dramatic form of a mundane truth.* "Templer has no ramp research" (batch 19 R1; a query containing "stair" returned stair papers — "R14 applied to everyone except myself"); "the predictor's first passed prospective test" (batch 17 §2; a screen artefact); "a false 200, the same shape batch 17 found on JSTOR" when the status was 403 (batch 18 §4d: "I upgraded a mundane block into the more alarming class"); "more permissive than the study its footnote rests on," "four independent sources," "no render existed" (batch 20).
- *A claim about what an instrument did, rather than what the bytes say.* "33 records, none architectural" with `rows=25`; `results_screened=43` hand-typed; "TRID reports 20 results" with no count in the artefact; "Google Books 0" from a 429; "SafetyLit 503" from `exit 35, 0 bytes`; "nine routes" for six body-capable requests. The self-pass re-reads the author's summary; the antagonist opens the manifest.
- *Corrections inherit the defect.* Batch 17 §9.1 "the retraction was itself unvalidated … the same defect as the first, one turn later" → ledger RULE 2026-09-18 "Self-correction is not self-verifying"; batch 20 §5 (its correction of GAP-037 was itself wrong); batch 18 §4c repeated batch 17's exact error "hours" after reading §9.4's retraction of it.
- *Late in the session.* Batch 17's first half "ran 4 and 0 and was closed as complete"; batch 19 §14 "the worst one was a gate I had just added"; batch 20 §0c's `open(p,"w").write(open(p).read())` truncation while repairing.

**Positioning.** The adversarial pass is not mandatory anywhere mechanical. `/batch-done` (`.claude/commands/batch-done.md`) runs `research_batch_dod.py` only; the Stop hook (`.claude/settings.json`) runs `research_batch_dod.py --all`; the harness-injected SessionStart contract text contains the word "adversarial" zero times; the registry's only "adversarial" entry, `audit_adversarial_use`, validates a misuse-vector catalogue for the guidebook's readers, not review of batches. DR-2026-08-19 §7's "optional single migration" — an `adversarial_findings` table in which `SURVIVED` rows are mandatory, "so a zero-finding pass is auditable rather than indistinguishable from a pass that never ran," which the DR calls "this repository's signature failure" — was never built (`sqlite_master` has no `%advers%` object). Recorded passes: batches 07, 08, 15, 17, 19, 20 — six of fifteen numbered September batches; 09–14, 16, 18 record none; batch 06 has no record at all and "never gets that audit." The `antagonist` agent is `model: fable` — the same class as the authoring sessions — so independence is a fresh context, not a different model (batch 20 §0's "a different model" is not accurate). And the fresh context is not reachable from every context that needs it: batch 20 "ran as a subagent with no agent-launching tool," so the pass could only happen after the coordinator noticed. DoD has reported COMPLIANT over broken provenance at least three times (batch 06 exec 44 with a count and no edge; batch 17's first half; batch 19 "19/19" with two headline findings false).

### Q5. Provenance modeling — the schema knows one way to find a source

Live schema (HEAD): `search_candidates.exec_id → search_executions` is the only typed discovery edge. `citation_mining` has FKs to `slugs` only; its discoveries are a JSON DOI list in `connections_produced`. `evidence_sources.derivation_chain` and `search_queries_used` exist, sit at 0 populated, and the pipeline contract's `discovery-provenance` criterion (`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml:141–152`) says "DO NOT ADD A WRITER WITHOUT SETTLING THE DUAL HOME FIRST" — the gap is named and frozen.

Recurrences of "filed on the nearest legal shape":

- Batch 17 §5: the Consensus search that surfaced two sources ran during a locator hunt and "I did not treat a locator hunt as a screening search"; candidates 107/108 hung off a ZERO YIELD exec; repaired by inventing exec 77 with `backfill=1` and prior "absent."
- Batch 17 §9.3: candidate 114 attributed to exec 75; true origin was reference 32 of REF-00986's deposit (a backward pass).
- GAP-050: Pinto from REF-01006's reference list; Templer from Internet Archive during an adversarial pass; both edges written to the nearest logged search.
- Backfill rows live: `select exec_id from search_executions where backfill=1` → 77, 87.
- DR-2026-08-19 §6 itself: `search_candidates` "requires `found_under_slug` and `session` NOT NULL — recovered leads have neither" — the instrument noticed the model could not hold a lead that did not come from a logged search, and widened `source_locators` instead of the model.

GAP-009/GAP-011 are the same shape one axis over: the schema assumed one source ↔ one slug (no writer for a second link; `add-source` named the correct action and could not perform it, batch 15 §5b), and the fix broke `citation_mining_completeness`, whose join ignores slug while `citation_mining` is keyed per `(slug, local_ref_id)` and `citation_mining_status` is one flag per source. Batch 08 (duplicate `local_ref_id` on retry → R2 unsatisfiable) and batch 16 (`log-mining` unable to express a ran-and-found-nothing pass; `deferred_reason` as the only notes channel) are further instances of the data model admitting fewer states than research produces. Each is filed as its own GAP; nobody has named the class.

### Q6. Unit-of-work shape

The evidence that the one-long-session shape contributes is the sessions' own testimony plus a consistent pattern, not a controlled comparison. Pattern: the code written in the last hour to fix what the batch found is what the next review finds broken — batch 15 §10, batch 17 §9.1, batch 19 §14 ("the worst one was a gate I had just added") and §15 ("three of the four hand-patches were the same anti-pattern the fix was for"), batch 20's three rounds. Testimony: batch 19 §15 "not at the end of a long session"; `workplan/adherence-attestation-build-2026-05-17.md:68` "Layer A discipline is the only defense; that defense degrades over long sessions"; `workplan/methodology-and-pipeline-enforcement-plan-2026-07-23.md:64` "Today only Claude's in-context attention orders the chain." Gap creation by day: 33 of 51 gaps on 2026-09-18, the day batches 13–18 ran; 43 of 51 gaps are OPEN — the same monotone curve DR §2.1 named for workplan markers (318→389→418), now in a table. The runbook prescribes the shape (§12.2 "Target (one long session)") and a ceiling ("Do not exceed … a failed batch of 30 remediates far worse than one of 10") that batches exceed on apparatus rather than admissions. Counter-evidence: mechanical defects are caught mid-session by gates (batch 19 §10 "all three were mine, all three were caught"; batch 14 §6 on-scratch gating). What escapes is interpretive, and interpretive claims are checked only by a second reader. Owner commentary on session length specifically: none found in the ledger; the owner's structural statements are model-routing (2026-07-25 class-not-version; 2026-09-11 "Fable to adjudicate … Opus to execute in agonist-antagonist method") and 2026-09-23 "stop running suites so frequently."

### Q7. Test-coverage gate for db.py refusals

The banner (`scripts/db.py:6880–6885`, "Every refusal here has a selftest case") has nothing behind it. `db.py` has no `--selftest`. The only test importing it is `test_db_integrity.py`, whose M02–M04 compare db.py's hand-writable field lists to the schema — not refusals. `run_checks.py --selftest` covers the registry; `research_batch_dod.py --selftest` seeds fixtures for the contract's R1–R15/R9a/R9b, not writer refusals; `dbcore --selftest` covers dbcore helpers. No mechanism fails when a writer ships without a test. Batch 20's `test_db_amend_writers.py` is registered **advisory** and covers only batch 20's verbs; the other ~40 writers remain uncovered. The one sweep that has repeatedly found writer defects is running the writers against a scratch DB (`derived_not_curated_audit.py:53–56` "which remains the only complete sweep"; batch 10 §Addendum "no check WRITES a search execution"; batch 20 §0c "Every correctness defect was found by running the code, not by any gate").

---

## 3. Root causes

**RC1. The gates verify that records agree with each other, never that a record agrees with the artefact — and because one code path writes both records, agreement is manufactured, not observed.**
Instances: batch 20 S01/`link-admission` (and the tuple-truth quote check, and the coincidental digit match); H05 rewriting seven research rows to stay green (2026-09-01/02); H01/H02's engine writing a JSON copy so the check would pass; CHECK 7 exempting the missing-edge case; `citation_mining_completeness` counting presence; batch 09's normaliser; the 2026-08-19 fabrication passing six "is it populated" gates.
Status: **(b)** named and partially fixed but recurring. CLAUDE.md rule 5 ("a parity check is not a fix"), §5(a), §5(c) name it; H01–H05 were deleted for it; S01 was then born (2026-09-18) with a comment conceding it is that shape, and a writer closed the loop. Nothing prevents a new parity-shaped check or a writer that copies the compared column.

**RC2. Every single-home derivation is opt-in per call site, the detector sees only two literal shapes and only after the column declares a CHECK, so under fix-forward pressure the literal wins and nothing goes red when it is written.**
Instances: batch 20 `amend_term` skipping `fk_declared`/`check_declared`; the DR's five-value disposition list; `results_admitted` as a "third store." Earlier: WRITABLE_TABLES ×8; B05/B06 tuples (batches 17, 19); `--verification-method` missing `direct-render`; `_CORRECTABLE` held to `_BIBLIO_FIELDS` by a comment; registry "N today" counts; rule 7a's own stale count; 26/51 `choices=` still literal; 26/46 writers using no derive helper; GAP-042.
Status: **(b)**. Rule 8 names it and dbcore supplies the helpers; `derived_not_curated_audit` is proactive for two shapes; sibling asymmetry has no detector, and a literal against a CHECK-less column is undetectable by design.

**RC3. Doctrine is spread over five stores with different mutation semantics and no currency index, so correctness depends on which subset a session read, and a superseded record is annotated only when the superseding session remembers.**
Instances: batch 20's step-7/H05 collision (24 days unrecorded) and the R13 contract line; DR-2026-08-24 §2.4 (overruled 2026-08-27, unannotated); DR-2026-07-22 (term ruled dead 2026-08-18, unannotated); DR-2026-05-09 (repointed by §7, unannotated); D-0170 vs D-0184 ("correctly citing a ratified DR while doing it"); DR-2026-08-19 §1.5's own "the DR was never annotated"; batch 13's false premise from a PR body; batch 10 correcting batch 09's record; 33/83 DRs annotated.
Status: **(a)/(b)**. Named in DR §0 (~30% correction commits), rule 0, rule 7a's "prose caller" clause, §6 "search both halves," and the 2026-09-11 ledger. Rule 0 and the append-only ledger partially address it; there is no index and the annotation step is manual.

**RC4. The only instrument that has ever caught an interpretive overclaim — a fresh reader going to the artefact — is optional, unregistered, invisible when absent, same-model as the author, and unreachable from the delegated contexts that actually run batches.**
Instances: batch 20 (self-pass 7 found / 21 missed; subagent could not launch the antagonist); the 2026-07-26 standard-form session was owner-prompted; batch 17 §9 "false in more places than §7 admitted, including inside the retraction"; batch 19 R1/R2 after DoD 19/19; batch 06 never audited; six of fifteen batches record a pass; `adversarial_findings` never built; DoD COMPLIANT over broken provenance three times.
Status: **(a)** named precisely in DR-2026-08-19 §7 and the ledger RULE "Self-correction is not self-verifying," but the mandatory-SURVIVED-rows mechanism was left "optional" and never landed; the pass never entered `/batch-done`, the Stop hook, or the registry.

**RC5. The data model admits one provenance shape — a pre-registered search surfaces a candidate that becomes one source on one slug — while research actually discovers sources through reference lists, locator hunts, archive browsing and adversarial passes, so each such discovery is filed on the nearest legal shape and the filing then reads as fact.**
Instances: GAP-050 and exec 87 (batch 20); exec 77 backfill and candidate 114 (batch 17); GAP-009/011; batch 08's `local_ref_id` collision; batch 16's inexpressible zero-yield mining pass; DR §6's `search_candidates` NOT NULLs. `citation_mining` has no FK to any search; `derivation_chain` is unreachable by contract.
Status: **(c)** never named as a class; each instance is its own GAP and the contract freezes the dual home rather than choosing the home.

**RC6. One session searches, screens, admits, extracts, grades, mines, self-reviews and repairs its own tooling, so the code most likely to be wrong — the writer or check written in the last hour — ships in the same PR as the research it was meant to protect.**
Instances: batch 20's three rounds each breaking the previous round's fix; batch 15 §10; batch 19 §14–15 and "not at the end of a long session"; batch 17's first half closed at 4/0; 33 gaps in one day.
Status: **(a)** named in May and July planning documents and by sessions themselves; never acted on — the runbook still prescribes "one long session."

---

## 4. The most load-bearing root cause

**RC4.** RC1 is the generating mechanism for the tautological greens, RC2 and RC5 for the drift and mis-filing, RC3 and RC6 for why sessions do not know better — but on this month's record, every instance of every one of them that was caught at all was caught by the same thing: a reader who had not written the claim, opening the artefact rather than the summary. That reader found S01's tautology (RC1), the hand-patched literals and `amend_term`'s missing gates (RC2), the step-7/H05 collision (RC3), GAP-050's fabricated provenance (RC5), and the last-hour fixes of batches 15/17/19/20 (RC6). Nothing else did. The DoD gate passed COMPLIANT over each. And the record shows what happens when that reader is absent: batch 06's admissions were never audited; batch 13 framed itself on a PR body; batch 10 designed against batch 09's wrong record; batch 20 inherited batch 19's unlogged reference-list step as an admission edge. An uncaught overclaim does not stay put — it becomes the next batch's premise, which is the recurrence the question asks about.

The mechanism to make that reader mandatory and its absence visible was fully specified on 2026-08-19 (§7: `adversarial_findings` with mandatory `SURVIVED` rows; `/batch-done` refusing without one for the session) and marked "optional." The one-sentence fix is that design, built, at blocking level, with `/batch-done` failing when the session has no findings row — which also makes the pass reachable from a delegated batch by making its absence the coordinator's problem rather than the subagent's. It is a detector, not a cure for RC1/RC2/RC5; but it is the only detector this repository has ever shown to work on the defects that matter, and it is currently run by memory in six batches out of fifteen.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- /home/user/guidebook/CLAUDE.md
- /home/user/guidebook/decisions/DR-2026-08-19-research-restart-operative-instrument.md
- /home/user/guidebook/scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py
- /home/user/guidebook/scripts/db.py
- /home/user/guidebook/governance/check-registry.yaml
- /home/user/guidebook/.claude/commands/batch-done.md

# Diagnostic survey: why the same defect shapes recur in the Guidebook's research pipeline

**Scope and method.** Read-only, 2026-09-26. Base is worktree HEAD `cf35d441` (main); the batch-20 specimen lives on branch `claude/batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa` (head `4f41b11b`), which I read via `git show`. The harness refused every `git show | python3` pipe, so I could not open the branch's DB; GAP-045..052 were read from the branch's data-migration SQL (`scripts/migrations/data_2026092[56]*.sql`), which is the only route rows take into the DB. Live counts below are from HEAD's `data/guidebook.db` opened `mode=ro`, or from `grep`/AST over HEAD's code. Every figure is measured today and will drift; the command is named where it matters. I read CLAUDE.md, DR-2026-08-19 (all 1,009 lines), the batch-20 record in full, batch records 06, 07, 10, 13, 17, 19 in full and 08, 09, 14, 15, 16, 18 in their self-review sections, the ledger tail (`references/project-standards.md` ~3560–3962 plus the 2026-09-11 entries), the check registry, `test_db_integrity.py` S01/H05, `derived_not_curated_audit.py`, `dbcore.writable_tables`, the `/adversarial`, `/batch-done` commands, the `antagonist` agent, and `.claude/settings.json` hooks.

---

## 1. The specimen, compressed to what it proves

Batch 20 (`sessions/session_2026-09-25-research-batch-20-audit-cluster-templer-fhwa.md`, branch only) went through three review rounds in ~24 hours:

- **Round 0 (self-pass, §0):** 7 defects found, 6 repaired. The self-pass "missed every one of the independent pass's findings."
- **Round 1 (independent antagonist, §0b):** 21 findings, including the headline "Table 13's band is more permissive than the study its footnote rests on" (true against one warrant, false against the other), "four independent sources" (a hand count including an abstract and a path-slope study), "no render of this page existed before" (false: batch 19's subagent rendered it and did not persist it). Also: the author's own pre-write quote checks tested a `(found, detail)` tuple's truth — vacuous for the whole batch.
- **Round 2 (code review, §0c):** the verb written in round 1 to satisfy S01 (`link-admission`) copies the very column S01 compares, so S01 cannot fail on anything it writes; the `--suggested-slug` fix was optional and existence-only; `amend-term` nested audit lines and skipped the `fk_declared`/`check_declared` gates its siblings apply; zero tests covered any new refusal; and `link-admission`'s `results_admitted` sync reintroduced a mechanism the 2026-09-02 repair had deliberately retired (H05). Verifying S01's edges then showed both copy proxy attributions: Pinto came from a reference list, Templer from an Internet Archive lookup during batch 19's adversarial pass — neither a logged search (GAP-050).

One document therefore contains: self-review that misses what a fresh reader catches; a repair that is tautological against the check it satisfies; a curated-gate omission in a sibling writer; a doctrine collision invisible to the author; a provenance model that cannot represent how two sources were actually found; and four review agents converging three times on one duplicated block.

---

## 2. Answers to the seven structural questions

### Q1. Self-validating checks — a class, not a one-off

S01 (`scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py:293–342`) compares `search_candidates.exec_id` with `search_admissions.exec_id`. `link_admission` (branch, `scripts/db.py`) refuses unless a candidate row records both ends, then writes that candidate's `exec_id` as the admission's `exec_id`. Agreement is manufactured by construction. S01's own comment already says the shape is "CLAUDE.md rule 5's shape — one fact with two homes"; it chose to police the dual home rather than remove it, and a verb closed the loop seven days later.

The same shape, on the record, before batch 20:

- **H05** (deleted 2026-09-02; comment at `test_db_integrity.py:1082–1095`): parity between `results_admitted` and `search_admissions`. "The gate did not detect drift; it CAUSED a research-stage record to be rewritten so the second home would agree with the first" — seven searches' counts set to 0 on 2026-09-01.
- **H01/H02** (deleted 2026-09-21, comment at `:1050–1056`): "the engine wrote the JSON copy SO THAT this check would pass, and assess_cell said so in its own comment."
- **H03/H04** (deleted 2026-08-24): same reason.
- **`research_protocol_audit` CHECK 7** (batch 17 §5): split its legacy exemption on `(r[2] or "") < "2026-09-03"`, and `''` is both a pre-cutoff row and a row with no admitting search — "every future source with a missing edge was exempted forever, by the check built to catch it."
- **`citation_mining_completeness`** (batch 16 §5b; ledger 2026-09-18): counts row presence, reporting "10/10 T1-2 sources mined, 100.0%" while 3 of 13 backward passes had run — the writer `log_mining` set `backward=1` unconditionally, including on deferrals.
- **Batch 09** (`session_2026-09-16-research-batch-09-…md:107–133`): `normalise_quote` reduced text to `[^0-9a-z]`, so an invented Japanese sentence "verified against the artefact." The anti-fabrication control was vacuous for six of nineteen languages.
- **Batch 20 §0**: the digit check accepted `1:12` against a sentence listing ramps "1, 4, 5, 9, 10, 11, 12" — satisfied by coincidence.
- **2026-08-19** (CLAUDE.md §5c): six gates passed fabricated co-authors "because each asked whether the author fields were populated, never whether they were true."

Would a registry review have caught S01? There is no such review. S01 is one of 62 `record()` ids under a single registry entry (`governance/check-registry.yaml:254`, `test_db_integrity`, `min_items: 1` for the whole battery). `run_checks.py --selftest` C1–C9 (`scripts/run_checks.py:666–815`) test registry coherence (unique ids, batteries declared, executables exist, classification, selection). Nothing anywhere reviews a check's logic against the writer whose output it examines. New db.py writers have landed in fix-forward commits inside research PRs in batches 15, 17, 19 and 20, and each was found defective by the next optional review (batch 15 §10: `link-source-slug` "collected the adjudication and recorded it never"; batch 19 §14: `journal_name` added to `_CORRECTABLE` broke the invariant in that constant's own header; batch 20 §0c above).

### Q2. Curated-list drift — the derived path is opt-in and blind at write time

Measured on HEAD (`scripts/db.py`): 51 `choices=` lists, 25 derived via `dbcore.schema_choices/check_values`, 26 literal. Of 46 writer-like functions (`def insert_|add_|log_|amend_|link_|resolve_|correct_|…`), 15 call `stamp_for`, 8 call `check_declared`/`check_values`, **2** call `fk_declared` (`amend_source`, `amend_extraction`), and 26 call none of the three. Still-curated module lists: `_AMENDABLE` (:3875), `_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS` (:6258), `_COVERAGE_COLS`, `_BPC_META_COLS`, `_VALID_DIRECTIONS`, `_VALID_CONFLICT_STATUS`, `_VALID_ITEM_STATUS`, `_VALID_RUN_STATUS`, `_PIPELINE_STEPS`, `_SVE_VOCAB_COLUMNS`. GAP-042 records four `evidence_sources` vocabularies that live only in a test file. GAP-013 records the `_AMENDABLE` inversion deferred because it was "a change to make deliberately, not at the end of a long session" (batch 19 §15).

Why it recurs, specifically:

1. **`derived_not_curated_audit.py`** (blocking) is proactive only for two shapes: an argparse `choices=` literal whose value set exactly equals a live CHECK, and a dict-literal row key absent from the schema. Its docstring (lines 49–56) states it cannot see `dict(data)`+subscript rows, cross-function assembly, or — the shape that recurred in batch 20 — a new writer omitting the gates its siblings apply. Nothing lints sibling asymmetry: `relate-extraction` lacked the `--verbatim-exempt` that `add-extraction` has (GAP-007, batch 13); `amend-search` could not record a late admission that `log-search` could (batch 09 §"Tooling defects"); `log-mining` could not express "ran and found nothing" (batch 16 §5); `amend_term` lacked `fk_declared`/`check_declared` (batch 20).
2. **A literal is invisible until the column declares a CHECK.** `check_declared` is a no-op on an unconstrained column, so "derived" silently degrades to unguarded (batch 19 §10a: `add-source --source-type` "accepted the bad value … because an undeclared vocabulary reads as no constraint"). The audit "went red in the same run" only when migration 091 added a CHECK (batch 19 §15) — proving the detector fires after the fact, on the schema change, not on the literal.
3. **The comment does not protect the reader.** WRITABLE_TABLES' eighth blindness "was added by the author who was reading those comments at the time" (CLAUDE.md rule 8); B05's curated tuple sat "eleven lines below" the comment recording B06's fix of the identical pattern (batch 19 §10a); rule 7a's stale count sits inside rule 7a; batch 19 records "rule 7a on its third outing in this batch."

### Q3. Doctrine currency — five stores, no index, annotation by habit

There is no "what is current" index. CLAUDE.md §9 points at DR-2026-08-19 for "what to do now" and the ledger tail for "latest rulings"; rule 0 says live rulings override on contact and §7 says "Owner rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`," which `.ignore` hides from the Grep tool. Doctrine therefore lives in: DRs (write-once, annotated when someone remembers), the ledger (append-only; rulings correct earlier rulings and, per the 2026-09-18 entry, their own snippets), CLAUDE.md (edited in place, history in git), code comments (GAP-051 cites "the H05 comment in `scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py`" as the record of the retirement), and session records (hidden from ripgrep). Correctness depends on which subset a session reads.

Unannotated supersessions I could confirm:

- **DR-2026-08-24 §2.4** ("Applicability is an OUTPUT of synthesis"): CLAUDE.md §6 says the owner overruled it on 2026-08-27. The DR carries a 2026-08-25 superseded-notice on a *different* section (line 229) and nothing on §2.4 (lines 285–312).
- **DR-2026-07-22-work-from-axes**: `axes` was ruled "a bad coined term … do not relitigate" on 2026-08-18 (CLAUDE.md rule 0 proof). Zero annotation in the DR.
- **DR-2026-05-09-adversarial-research-protocol**: "Supersedes: None"; DR-2026-08-19 §7 "repointed" adversarial review. Zero annotation.
- **DR-2026-08-19 step 7** ("in one transaction: UPDATE search_executions SET … results_admitted") vs the 2026-09-02 H05 retirement: the repair session (`sessions/session_2026-09-02-owed-repairs.md:47`) never cites the DR; the collision was found 24 days later by a code review, and the DR was not annotated even then (GAP-051 instead).
- **`governance/research-contract.yaml:229–231`** ("no-participants = PROXY") vs DR-2026-08-19's R13 text: found 2026-09-25; the ruling supersedes it "as applied", and the line was deliberately left in place.
- **D-0170 vs D-0184** (ledger 2026-09-11): "A session reading D-0170 alone would have built the wrong thing, correctly citing a ratified DR while doing it."
- **DR-2026-08-19 §1.5** already documents this for DR-2026-08-06 §3: "That reasoning no longer holds, and the DR was never annotated."

Census: 83 DRs, 33 contain any supersession/amendment wording (`grep -il 'superseded by|overruled|AMENDED 20|STRUCK 20|CORRECTION' decisions/DR-*.md`). The operative instrument itself — written to end the "re-derive, re-litigate, re-render" recursion its §0 measured at ~30% of commits — has been amended in place at least six times (08-22, 08-23, 08-25, 09-02, 09-10, 09-26), and its §12.1 is "SUPERSEDED 2026-09-10 — see `workplan/2026-09-10-batch-06-runbook.md`," a fifth document its §8 says may not exist.

### Q4. Why self-review fails the same way, and where the adversarial pass sits

**The shape of what self-review misses** is consistent across batches 17, 19 and 20:

- *The more dramatic form of a mundane truth.* "Templer has no ramp research" (batch 19 R1; a query containing "stair" returned stair papers — "R14 applied to everyone except myself"); "the predictor's first passed prospective test" (batch 17 §2; a screen artefact); "a false 200, the same shape batch 17 found on JSTOR" when the status was 403 (batch 18 §4d: "I upgraded a mundane block into the more alarming class"); "more permissive than the study its footnote rests on," "four independent sources," "no render existed" (batch 20).
- *A claim about what an instrument did, rather than what the bytes say.* "33 records, none architectural" with `rows=25`; `results_screened=43` hand-typed; "TRID reports 20 results" with no count in the artefact; "Google Books 0" from a 429; "SafetyLit 503" from `exit 35, 0 bytes`; "nine routes" for six body-capable requests. The self-pass re-reads the author's summary; the antagonist opens the manifest.
- *Corrections inherit the defect.* Batch 17 §9.1 "the retraction was itself unvalidated … the same defect as the first, one turn later" → ledger RULE 2026-09-18 "Self-correction is not self-verifying"; batch 20 §5 (its correction of GAP-037 was itself wrong); batch 18 §4c repeated batch 17's exact error "hours" after reading §9.4's retraction of it.
- *Late in the session.* Batch 17's first half "ran 4 and 0 and was closed as complete"; batch 19 §14 "the worst one was a gate I had just added"; batch 20 §0c's `open(p,"w").write(open(p).read())` truncation while repairing.

**Positioning.** The adversarial pass is not mandatory anywhere mechanical. `/batch-done` (`.claude/commands/batch-done.md`) runs `research_batch_dod.py` only; the Stop hook (`.claude/settings.json`) runs `research_batch_dod.py --all`; the harness-injected SessionStart contract text contains the word "adversarial" zero times; the registry's only "adversarial" entry, `audit_adversarial_use`, validates a misuse-vector catalogue for the guidebook's readers, not review of batches. DR-2026-08-19 §7's "optional single migration" — an `adversarial_findings` table in which `SURVIVED` rows are mandatory, "so a zero-finding pass is auditable rather than indistinguishable from a pass that never ran," which the DR calls "this repository's signature failure" — was never built (`sqlite_master` has no `%advers%` object). Recorded passes: batches 07, 08, 15, 17, 19, 20 — six of fifteen numbered September batches; 09–14, 16, 18 record none; batch 06 has no record at all and "never gets that audit." The `antagonist` agent is `model: fable` — the same class as the authoring sessions — so independence is a fresh context, not a different model (batch 20 §0's "a different model" is not accurate). And the fresh context is not reachable from every context that needs it: batch 20 "ran as a subagent with no agent-launching tool," so the pass could only happen after the coordinator noticed. DoD has reported COMPLIANT over broken provenance at least three times (batch 06 exec 44 with a count and no edge; batch 17's first half; batch 19 "19/19" with two headline findings false).

### Q5. Provenance modeling — the schema knows one way to find a source

Live schema (HEAD): `search_candidates.exec_id → search_executions` is the only typed discovery edge. `citation_mining` has FKs to `slugs` only; its discoveries are a JSON DOI list in `connections_produced`. `evidence_sources.derivation_chain` and `search_queries_used` exist, sit at 0 populated, and the pipeline contract's `discovery-provenance` criterion (`governance/pipeline-contract.yaml:141–152`) says "DO NOT ADD A WRITER WITHOUT SETTLING THE DUAL HOME FIRST" — the gap is named and frozen.

Recurrences of "filed on the nearest legal shape":

- Batch 17 §5: the Consensus search that surfaced two sources ran during a locator hunt and "I did not treat a locator hunt as a screening search"; candidates 107/108 hung off a ZERO YIELD exec; repaired by inventing exec 77 with `backfill=1` and prior "absent."
- Batch 17 §9.3: candidate 114 attributed to exec 75; true origin was reference 32 of REF-00986's deposit (a backward pass).
- GAP-050: Pinto from REF-01006's reference list; Templer from Internet Archive during an adversarial pass; both edges written to the nearest logged search.
- Backfill rows live: `select exec_id from search_executions where backfill=1` → 77, 87.
- DR-2026-08-19 §6 itself: `search_candidates` "requires `found_under_slug` and `session` NOT NULL — recovered leads have neither" — the instrument noticed the model could not hold a lead that did not come from a logged search, and widened `source_locators` instead of the model.

GAP-009/GAP-011 are the same shape one axis over: the schema assumed one source ↔ one slug (no writer for a second link; `add-source` named the correct action and could not perform it, batch 15 §5b), and the fix broke `citation_mining_completeness`, whose join ignores slug while `citation_mining` is keyed per `(slug, local_ref_id)` and `citation_mining_status` is one flag per source. Batch 08 (duplicate `local_ref_id` on retry → R2 unsatisfiable) and batch 16 (`log-mining` unable to express a ran-and-found-nothing pass; `deferred_reason` as the only notes channel) are further instances of the data model admitting fewer states than research produces. Each is filed as its own GAP; nobody has named the class.

### Q6. Unit-of-work shape

The evidence that the one-long-session shape contributes is the sessions' own testimony plus a consistent pattern, not a controlled comparison. Pattern: the code written in the last hour to fix what the batch found is what the next review finds broken — batch 15 §10, batch 17 §9.1, batch 19 §14 ("the worst one was a gate I had just added") and §15 ("three of the four hand-patches were the same anti-pattern the fix was for"), batch 20's three rounds. ## 4. The most load-bearing root cause

**RC4.** RC1 is the generating mechanism for the tautological greens, RC2 and RC5 for the drift and mis-filing, RC3 and RC6 for why sessions do not know better — but on this month's record, every instance of every one of them that was caught at all was caught by the same thing: a reader who had not written the claim, opening the artefact rather than the summary. That reader found S01's tautology (RC1), the hand-patched literals and `amend_term`'s missing gates (RC2), the step-7/H05 collision (RC3), GAP-050's fabricated provenance (RC5), and the last-hour fixes of batches 15/17/19/20 (RC6). Nothing else did. The DoD gate passed COMPLIANT over each. And the record shows what happens when that reader is absent: batch 06's admissions were never audited; batch 13 framed itself on a PR body; batch 10 designed against batch 09's wrong record; batch 20 inherited batch 19's unlogged reference-list step as an admission edge. An uncaught overclaim does not stay put — it becomes the next batch's premise, which is the recurrence the question asks about.

The mechanism to make that reader mandatory and its absence visible was fully specified on 2026-08-19 (§7: `adversarial_findings` with mandatory `SURVIVED` rows; `/batch-done` refusing without one for the session) and marked "optional." The one-sentence fix is that design, built, at blocking level, with `/batch-done` failing when the session has no findings row — which also makes the pass reachable from a delegated batch by making its absence the coordinator's problem rather than the subagent's. It is a detector, not a cure for RC1/RC2/RC5; but it is the only detector this repository has ever shown to work on the defects that matter, and it is currently run by memory in six batches out of fifteen.
